parties:
Karamat Ali and others ------ Petitioners
vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
But this case is not applicable in the present cases as because that was a case regarding retirement of Government employee and there was no guideline or Rules and the facts are also distinguishable. In this regard Mr. Additional Attorney-General submits that Article 25 of President's Order 16 of 1972 clearly provides that the Government may make rules for carrying out the purposes of the order and in exercise of such power Government has framed the notice in the form in exercise of the power vested under Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Taking over Possession) Rules 1972 and in Rule 6 residential and other buildings in the urban area have been classified as one category of abandoned property. For taking over possession of abandoned property, notice in Forms I, II, III & IV, as, the case may be, can be issued. The learned Additional Attorney-General submits that notice in any form means, depending on the category of abandoned property and notice in any form of the specimen given as per Rule 3 should be issued before taking over of the abandoned property. So, there is no violation of any law and it was nor arbitrary. Mr Farooqui referring to section 4(b) (ii) of Ordinance 54 of 1985 next contends that no building shall be taken possession of as abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972 except in pursuance of a notice in any form issued under President's Order 16 of 1972 and where no such notice is issued in respect of a building, in execution of a decree or order passed by a Court in a suit filed by the government. He submits that this is clear discrimination in equality and is hit by equality clause under Articles 27 and 31 of our Constitution. He submits that thereby classification has been made by this Ordinance. He further submits that the Government may institute suit for recovery of abandoned property if those were not included in the list. He next submits that equals are not being treated equally. So, it offends the fundamental right of equality clause as guaranteed under Article 27 of the Constitution. Mr Farooqui then cited a number of decisions but we shall refer only to the relevant ones. In support of his contention he referred the case of Jibendra Kishore Acharyya Chowdhury and 58 others vs. Province of East Pakistan and Secretary, Finance and Revenue Department, Government of East Pakistan, reported in 9 DLR (SC) 21. We have gone through the decision very minutely and find that it is quite distinguishable and the principles, facts and circumstances are not applicable in the present case. He referred to the case of Waris Meah vs. State, reported in PLD 1957 (SC) 157 and submits that establishment of the Court of Settlement by Ordinance 54/85 created discrimination giving right to the government to go to the civil Court for recovery of possession of any abandoned property and debarring the other claimants to establish their claims. In this case it has been held that the Foreign Exchange Regulation(Amendment) Act (XXXII of 1956), which by adding sections 22A, 23(A) and 23B to the original Act gave power to the Central Government or the State Bank to determine whether an offender, under the original Act was to be tried under the ordinary law (section 23), Or by an Adjudication Officer (section 23A), or by a Tribunal (section 23B) and the three sections preserving three different punishing authorities each with different power and procedure and entailing punishments of unequal nature and description, offended against Article 5 of the Constitution and was for that reason void. The amending Act makes the principal Act ex-facie discriminatory and infringes the subject''''s fundamental right to equal protection of the law guaranteed by Article 5 of the Constitution of Pakistan." 

 28. From the respective submissions of the parties in this case the question before us is whether the guarantee of the Constitution, in Article 27, that "all citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law" has been disregarded in the impugned legislation, namely, section 7(2)(g) of the Union Parishad Ordinance. First of all, it is to be clearly understood what ''''the equality of law'''' means. Sir Ivor Jennings in his "The Law and the Constitution" has stated: 

 "Once a building is included in the list of abandoned properties it is conclusive, evidence that the building in question is an abandoned property where the owner either was not present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were not known or he eased to manage or occupy the property at the time when President's Order 16 of 1972 was promulgated on 16-2-1972. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable one. It is for the claimant to show that the original owner was present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or he did not cease to occupy or manage the property in question at the relevant time. Since the notification in the official Gazette carries a presumption that the building in question is in abandoned property, it is exempt from any legal process be it an auction sale by the Government itself or through court" 

 "9. Admittedly, the property has been listed as an abandoned property. Thus the onus lies upon the petitioner to the but the presumption, provided in sub-section (2) of sections 5 that the same was not an abandoned property. No oral evidence has been adduced before the Settlement Court to prove that on 26-2-72 when President''''s Order 16 of 1972 was promulgated the original lessee, Naimuddin had been present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or that he did not cease to occupy, supervise or manage in person the house in question. The Settlement Court upon assigning cogent reasons held that the kabala of the petitioner's vendor is a forged and fabricated document and the original lessee, Naimuddin did never appear physically before any authority for any purpose after the liberation war in Bangladesh. The High Court Division has thus, rightly, maintained the order of the Settlement Court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 "No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence, the listing of the property as an abandoned property in the Supplementary Provisions Ordinance, 1985 was lawful as it was ail abandoned property by operation of law." 

 24. We find that the Settlement Court upon consideration of oral and documentary evidence came to the finding that Zakia Khatoon, the vendor of the petitioner, was a fake person who did not purchase the land from original owner Rafi Ahmed Fidal. Zakia Khatoon was not examined in this case before the Court of Settlement and no evidence came before the court that Zakia Khatoon died and Settlement Court also found that L TI of Zakia Khatoon in the first page of the Kabala executed in favour of Ambia Khatoon does not tally with LTI in the rest of the pages and the expert opined in the similar way. The Settlement Court also came to a finding that the fact that Zakia Khatoon was a fictitious person. So the question of purchase of the case property by Jakia Khatoon on 6th June, 1963 does not arise. Accordingly, the purchase of the case property by the present petitioner from her does not arise. Her kabala and the kabala in the name of Jakia are products of false personation. All these are findings of fact and in a petition of certiorari we cannot look into it. The findings of the Court of Settlement are based on facts and materials produced before it. This court could interfere with the findings of fact under its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution only if it could be shown that the tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence and facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted malafide or in violation of any principle of natural justice. In the case of Mostafa Kamal (Md) vs. First Court of Settlement and others, reported in 48 DLR (AD) 61 relevant paragraph 4 wherein it has been held: 

 "4. Court of Settlement on consideration of the materials on record arrived at a finding that Nasima Khatun is not the daughter and heir of original lessee Mobina Khatun and that the said lessee had not been in possession of the house in question at the relevant time. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon taking into consideration of such clear finding of facts of the Court of Settlement refused rightly to interfere with the judgment of that court upon a correct appreciation of the legal principle that the High Court Division in exercise of its writ jurisdiction can not sit as a Court of Appeal over the judgment of the Court of Settlement for resettling questions of fact. Thus we find no illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division." 

 "6…………………..In exercising the jurisdiction in certiorari the learned Judges sat over the judgment of the Tribunal as a court of appeal and reversed the findings of fact of the Court of Settlement. The learned Judges on consideration of the materials and evidences on record took a different view that Md Nasim was the son of original allottee Yahiya as the original title deed and original receipts showing payment of rent, taxes, etc. were produced from the custody of respondent No. 1. The learned Judges relied very much on this circumstantial evidence. The learned Judges also found that respondent No.1 having failed to give the exact date of death does not ipso facto disprove the assertion that Yahiya died some time in 1970. 

 28. The case of the petitioner is that, the case property consisting of 2 storied building previously belonged to one Md Humayun Mirza by virtue of purchase from Md Kashem on 21-6-63. The said purchaser executed power of attorney in favour of Anisur Rahman and got it registered on 24-3-73 and thereby appointed Anisur Rahman to manage the property and sell out same on his behalf, if necessary. Humayun Mirza started a hotel in the case property in the year 1974 on obtaining permission of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. Thereafter he sold the property to Nuruzzaman by a registered kabala dated 10-3-73 and delivered possession to the purchaser. The purchaser Md Nuruzzaman mortgaged the property with the Pubali Bank for taking loan. Thereafter Md Nuruzzaman executed a bainapatra in favour of the petitioner Abu Naser Siddique on 19-9-78 for sale of the case property for a consideration of Taka 1,60,000.00. The vendor Nuruzzaman received Taka 50,000.00 as advance but did not execute kabala. Again Nazrnul Huq, brother of Nuruzzaman, executed another bainapatra on behalf of his brother on 18-10-78 and received Taka 1,00,000.00. The petitioner filed Title Suit No. 1262 of 1980 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Nuruzzaman for specific performance of contract and the suit was decreed ex parte on 16-1-83. In pursuance of the ex parte decree, the petitioner got kabala executed and registered through court on 9-7-86 and in this way the petitioner has become owner of the property but it has been wrongly treated as abandoned property performance of contract and the suit was decreed ex parte on 16-1-83. In pursuance of the ex parte decree, the petitioner got kabala executed and registered through court on 9-7-86 and in this way the petitioner has become owner of the property but it has been wrongly treated as abandoned property. 

 31. Mr MI Farooqui the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the Court of Settlement, on a wrong interpretation and construction of law relating to citizenship, committed an error of law in finding that Mirza Humayun, the admitted original owner, is a citizen of a State which was at war and engaged in military operation against Bangladesh during the war of liberation. He next contends that the property, from the facts and evidence adduced on behalf of the petitioner, is not an abandoned property. The settlement court erred in law in not excluding it from the abandoned list. 

 "6....... In exercising the jurisdiction in certiorari the learned Judges sat over the judgment of the Tribunal as a court of appeal and reversed the findings of facts of the Court of Settlement The learned Judges on consideration of the materials and evidences on record took a different view that Md Nasim was the son of original allottee Yahiya as the original title deed and original receipts showing payment of rent, taxes, etc. were produced from the custody of respondent No. 1. The learned Judges relied very much on this circumstantial evidence. The learned Judges also found that respondent No.1 having failed to give the exact date of death does not ipso facto disprove the assertion that Yahiya died some time in 1970. The manner in which the learned Judges considered the material on record is, in fact, the manner in which a court of appeal disposes of an appeal. The learned Judges of the High Court Division exceeded their jurisdiction while exercising their power under certiorari to interfere with the judgment of an inferior tribunal." 

 39. The case of the petitioner Dr Fakir Anjuman Ara is that she acquired title in the property on the basis of purchase from the previous owner Sk Jalil, who got allotment of the suit property as relief plot from the then Government of East Pakistan. Sk Jalil the owner entered into an agreement for sale of the case plot to one Abdus Salam who filed title suit No. 542 of 1974 against Sk. Jalil for specific performance of contract and on 31- 7 -79 got an ex parte decree. A kabala was also executed and registered through court on 11-6-80. The decree holder Abdus Salam transferred the case property to Golam Haider and others on 30-5-83 and subsequently on 31-10-84, the case property was again transferred to the petitioner by another kabala and the petitioner is now in possession. 

 40. Respondent No. 1 opposes the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying all material  allegations contending, inter alia, that Sk. Jalil, the original lessee, never entered into any agreement for sale of the case property with Abdus Salam on 5-12-70 and the said agreement is false, forged, fabricated, ante-dated, without consideration and said Abdus Salam brought a false suit being No. 542 of 1974 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Sk Jalil for specific performance of contract by suppression of all material facts and Sk. Jalil never died here in Bangladesh on 28-4-76 or Matoon Bibi was not the wife of said Sk Jalil. Abdus Salam obtained an ex parte decree on 31-7-79 and got a registered sale deed through court on 11-6-80 by playing fraud upon the court and subsequent transfer by Abdus Salam in favour of Golam Haider and his wife Momtaj Begum on 30-5-83 are also false, forged, fraudulent, without consideration. It is further submitted that Sk. Jalil was an immigrant and the case plot was allotted to him for his rehabilitation and during liberation war and afterwards, the whereabouts of said Sk. Jalil and members of his family were not known and they ceased to occupy, manage and supervise the case property in person. Hence the case property absolutely vested in the Government as abandoned property. 

 44. It appears that the Title Suit No. 542 of 1974 was filed against Sk Jalil for specific performance of contract and since Sk Jalil did not appear the case was decreed ex parte but the petitioner could not produce any acceptable evidence to prove that Sk Jalil lived in this country after 1971 and died in the country in the year 1975-76. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted before the Settlement Court that Sk Jalil died in the year 1974. It appears that the Court of Settlement on proper consideration of the evidence on record including the photo copy of death certificate Annexure-G, wherein the date of death is totally illegible and came to the finding that the death certificate is a false one. It appears that on perusal of the Government file the learned Settlement Court found that as per burial certificate produced earlier shows he died on 26-12-77 but in the suit for specific performance of contract the date of death was shown on 20-7-76. So it appears that the Court of Settlement correctly found that the date of death of Sk Jalil cannot be relied upon. It further appears that the Settlement Court also on proper consideration of the facts, circumstances and papers available produced before it and from the Government file rightly held that the admitted owner Jalil did not possess the case land at the relevant time or after the commencement of the President''''s Order 16 of 1972. He was neither available in the country nor there is any evidence to show that he accepted citizenship of this country. Therefore, the Government after getting report of the survey team has rightly served notice on the unauthorised occupants of the house in the absence of the original owner and the case property has rightly vested in the government. Now the assertion of the petitioner that in pursuance of the ex parte decree he is in possession is of no avail. In the case of CQMH Md Ayub Ali vs. Bangladesh and others, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 relevant paragraph 26 wherein it has been held: 

 "6 ………………………….In exercising the jurisdiction in certiorari the learned Judges sat over the judgment of the tribunal as a court of appeal and reversed the findings of fact of the Court of Settlement. The learned Judges on consideration of the materials and evidence on record took a different view that Md. Nasim was the son of original allottee Yahiya as the original title deed and original receipts showing payment of rent, taxes, etc. were produced from the custody of respondent No. 1. The learned Judges relied very much on this circumstantial evidence. The learned Judges also found that respondent No. 1 having failed to give the exact date of death does not ipso facto disprove the assertion that Yahiya died some time in 1970. The manner in which the learned judges considered the material on record is in fact the manner in which a court of appeal disposes of an appeal. The learned Judges of the High Court Division exceeded their jurisdiction while exercising their power under certiorari to interfere with the judgment of an inferior tribunal." 

 48. The case of the petitioner Fatema Khatun is that the case property previously belonged to Iqbal Ali Khan who took lease of the same from the then Government of East Pakistan by registered deed of lease on 15-1-60. While in possession, the lessee-owner Iqbal AIi Khan entered into an agreement for sale of the case property with the petitioner on 5-1-71. The vendor of the case house did not execute and register the deed of sale and, as such, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 1095 of 1981 on 16-9-81 and got an ex parte decree on 20-6-83 and the sale deed was executed and registered through court on 29-9-83 and the petitioner has been possessing the property since agreement for sale on 5-1-71. The Government had never taken over possession of the case house and the petitioner and the lessee-owner Iqbal Ali Khan were in possession of the case property immediately before commencement of President's Order 16 of 1972. The case house is not an abandoned property. The, petitioner applied to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works for release of the case house from the list of the abandoned buildings which was subsequently heard by the Settlement Court. 

 51. Mr MI Farooqui, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits chat Settlement Court based its judgment on Annexures-B and B1 without taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and representation made earlier by the petitioner and thus acted without any lawful authority. He submits that the Settlement'''' Court on mere conjecture and surmises held that the petitioner created forged deed of agreement for sale and without examining the signature of the vendor on the agreement of the lease deed and thus committed an error of law. He next contended that in pursuance of the decree the petitioner is in possession and the government is estopped from denying the title of the petitioner. 

 53. It is submitted that admittedly the lessee Iqbal Ali Khan was not available in Bangladesh immediately after the liberation of Bangladesh in 1971. His whereabouts were not known to the Government. The case house became abandoned one and vested in the Government and the Government manages and controls the house by giving allotment issuing demand notice to QG Mostafa. It is further submitted that the petitioner has no interest in the suit property. The alleged agreement for sale is false and fraudulent and the petitioner obtained sale deed through court on the basis of false and fraudulent agreement and cannot claim title over the property in pursuance of the decree. 

 54. It appears that the petitioner claims ownership in the case property on the basis of agreement for sale between Iqbal Ali Khan and petitioner and the sale deed executed and registered through court in pursuance of the ex parte decree dated 20-6-83 in Title Suit No. 1095 of 1981 but the Settlement Court found from the document of QG Mostafa, the admitted husband of the petitioner, by his application dated 9-2-76 and 19-8-76 admitted the case property as abandoned property and prayed for allotment of the same, either in his favour or in favour of his wife Mrs. Fatema and the Government accordingly allotted the same in the name of his wife the petitioner. It further appears that the Settlement Court on perusal of the Government record found that the petitioner's husband filed an application dated 11-6-86 after return from Pakistan in 1973 and took over possession of the house with the help of some students. On such facts the Settlement Court found the agreement for sale in respect of case property as a forged one as her husband filed an application for taking lease admitting the property as abandoned property. It further appears that as per direction of the Court of Settlement QG Mostafa gave three English and Bengali specimen signatures and the court compared those with the other signatures available in the above mentioned applications and found that the signatures tally with each other and they are the products of the same and one hand. Thus the Settlement Court also found that the petitioner filed this case on false ground and claim of ownership of the case property with malafide intention to grab this property. On such facts discussed above we find that admittedly the petitioner's husband applied for lease of the property as abandoned property. The assertion of the petitioner on the basis of the ex parte decree is not tenable in law. In the case of CQMH Md Ayub Ali vs. Bangladesh and others, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 relevant paragraph 26 wherein it has been held: 

 "6…………………..In exercising the jurisdiction in certiorari the learned Judges sat over the judgment of the Tribunal as a court of appeal and reversed the findings of fact of the Court of Settlement. The learned Judges on consideration of the materials and evidence on record took a different view that Md Nasim was the son of original allottee Yahiya as the original title deed and original receipts showing payment of rent, taxes, etc. were produced from the custody of respondent No. 1. The learned Judges relied very much on this circumstantial evidence. The learned Judges also found that respondent No.1 having failed to give the exact date of death does not ipso facto disprove the assertion that Yahiya died some time in 1970. The manner in which the learned Judges considered the material on record is in fact the manner in which a court of appeal disposes of an appeal. The learned Judges of the High Court Division exceeded their jurisdiction while exercising their power under certiorari to interfere with the judgment of an inferior tribunal." 

 57. The case of the petitioners is that, Mrs. Amina Khatun predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner, obtained 99 years leasehold right along with the possession of the plot No. CES(b) CYC 284 Road No.117 from the Dhaka Improvement Trust with such terms and conditions as described in the standard lease agreement dated 17-3-61 upon payment of full consideration amount. The original lease deed is annexure B to this petition. The aforesaid Amina Khatun with a view to transferring her property to the petitioners filed a written application on 1-1-72 under the relevant provision of the original lease agreement dated 17-3-61, with the DIT. She was allowed to transfer the suit plot vide permission No. DIT/No. 5 dated 1-1-73 issued by the Estate Officer, the respondent No.2. A photo copy of the said permission is Annexure-''A''. It is stated that at the relevant time ie 1st January, 1973 the transferor Mrs Amena Khatun the original lease holder was a citizen of Bangladesh and she sold the said plot with prior permission dated 1-1-73 to the petitioners; The original lessee paid Taka 6.760.00 in favour of the respondent No. 2 as transfer fee for transferring the plot in question in favour of the. petitioners. A photo copy of the said receipt of the petitioners of the said amount as transfer fee is annexed hereto and marked as Annexure-''C''. On completion of all legal formalities the petitioners obtained the deed of sale from the original lessee on 28-2-73. The sale deed for an amount of Taka 99,0002,00 is Annexure-''D'' to this petition. Thereafter the petitioners applied for mutation of their names which was allowed by the respondents and other authorities as would be evident from Memo dated 2-5-73, 2-10-88 and 4-10-88 vide Annexures-E, E-1, & E-2 respectively. The petitioners then applied to the DIT for permission to mortgage their property for securing loan from Pubali Bank, Motijheel Branch, Dhaka and the petitioners were allowed permission vide Memo dated 21-11-80 Annexure-F to this petition. The petitioners are also paying municipal taxes, income taxes and other taxes regularly and thereby asserting their right of ownerships and possession without any interruption from any quarters including the respondents. The petitioners while in such possession recently applied to the DIT for partition of their properties and they were informed that the Ministry of Works most illegally and arbitrarily listed the properties in ''''Kha'''' list of the abandoned property beyond their knowledge when admittedly the petitioners are in possession of the property and, as such the listing of the petitioners property as abandoned property is illegal as no notice was served till to-day for listing the same as abandoned property, which is a condition precedent for inclusion of the same in the list of the abandoned properties as contemplated under sections 4 and 5 of Ordinance 54 of 1985. By supplementary affidavit the petitioners asserted that while the petitioners came to  learn in early part of April, 1996 that the   property had been listed in the ''Kha'' list as aforesaid, the petitioners together with Mr Khandker Mojibur Rahman, husband of the petitioner No.1, went to the Settlement Court No. 1, Dhaka on 8-4-96 for filing a case to release the property from the list of abandoned building but they were informed by the Registrar of the said Settlement Court that since the time to file such case had expired long ago the Settlement Court would not accept any new case. Whereupon the petitioners solicited advice of Sharif and Nabi, Advocates who advised for filing a writ petition. It is further stated that in the supplementary affidavit that the Original Title Deeds and connected documents of the petitioners are at the moment deposited with the Pubali Bank, Head Office, there being a mortgage of the case building for further construction. The copies of the letters of the Pubali Bank are annexed herewith and marked as Annexures- K and K-1. 

 58. Respondent No. 1 contested the petition by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying all  material assertions contending, inter alia that the original owner Amena Khatun left this country prior to promulgation of President's Order 16 of 1972 and left the property uncared for arid her whereabouts were not known. So the alleged sale deed dated 28-2-73 is a false and concocted one and was created in order to grab the valuable properties' of the Government. It is also stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that since the petitioners are not the owners of the property no notice was required to be served upon them since the original owner left the country keeping the property uncared for and ceased to occupy, supervise or manage in person the property and the property was rightly declared as abandoned. It is further stated that Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 is a beneficial legislation and very much constitutional. It is further stated that this Writ Petition is not maintainable as because the Court of Settlement has got exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate the matter-relating to exclusion of the property from abandoned list and since the petitioner had never gone to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the property from the list of abandoned property as provided under Ordinance 54 of 1985 the instant Writ Petition is not maintainable. It. is further stated that the petitioner has never gone to the Court of Settlement to seek redress inasmuch as nobody is required to go to the Registrar of the Court of Settlement for filing cases, as the functions of the Registrar do not relate to filing of cases, rather the function of the registrar is administrative in nature. 

 "The petitioner is entitled to challenge the inclusion of her house in the ''Ka'' list of abandoned buildings by way of the Court's writ jurisdiction of this court in spite of dismissal of her application by the Court of Settlement on the ground of limitation". 

 63. It is also not denied by the respondent that Amena Khatoon, original lessee of the plot, was a citizen of erstwhile East Pakistan and at the relevant time and with permission dated 1-1-73 sold the same to the petitioners by a registered deed of sale and she also paid the transfer fee of Taka 6,700.00 in favour of respondent No. 2 Annexure-A' and 'C' respectively. It is also not denied that after registration of sale deed dated 18-2-73 Annexure-'D' the petitioners mutated their names with Rajuk and other authorities as would be evident from Memo dated 2-5-73, 2-10-88 vide Annexures E, E-1 and E-2, and that the petitioners applied to the Rajuk for permission to mortgage the property for securing loan from Pubali Bank, Motijheel Branch, Dhaka which was allowed vide Memo dated 21-11-80 Annexure-F and that the petitioners have been in possession of the property by paying taxes revenues, etc. without any interruption from any quarter whatsoever, and that for the first time they came to know that their property had been listed in 'Kha' list as abandoned property when they filed application for partition of the plot in April 1986. From these admitted facts without going into further details we also find that the property in question has been illegally listed in 'Kha' list as it does not come within the mischief of any provision of 16 of 1972 or Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 and of no legal effect.

parties:
Nasir Hossain (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh, Bangladesh Secretariat and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. One Hosne Ali got the case property by the way of lease from the Government of erstwhile East Pakistan vide registered deed No. 3216 dated 5-4-1962 and being in right title and possession sold it to Md Zahoor by registered kabala dated 3-1-64 who in turn sold if to Chand Mia vide registered Kabala dated 7-10-74. Thereafter, one Laila Bilkis Banoo by a registered Kabala purchased the case property on 7-11-76 from Chand Mia and thereafter the former (Laiia Bilkis Banoo) sold to the present Writ Petitioner vide registered deeds dated 14-7-86 and 16-7-86 and since then he has been possessing the same in his own right and the petitioner as well as the previous vendor referred to above are Bangladeshi citizens and never left the country and for which there is no reason or occasion to treat the case property as abandoned but unfortunately, the Government has included the property in 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings by publishing an Additional Gazette on 26-12-88 behind the back of petitioner. 

 5. We have heard Mr Kazi Abdul Wahab, the learned Advocate for the writ petitioner as well as the Annexures referred thereto. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submitted that the Court of Settlement arrived at a decision on guess and surmise. He also submitted that the Court of Settlement failed to consider that the Government permitted the mutation as well as transfer of the case property to the petitioner and to his predecessor-in- interest. The certified copies of the title deeds of the vendor of the petitioner chrono logically proved the valid title of the petitioner and there is no reason to disbelieve the same. He further submitted that the Court of Settlement failed to controvert the documentary evidence filed in support of the transfer stage by stage but merely relied on the facts that the original documents of title have not been filed without considering the fact that there may be hundred and one grounds for absence of the original title deeds since great war of liberation took place in the meantime which had made the life of the inhabitants of this country, specially the inhabitants of the area where the case property, situates topsy turvy and, as such, it is not unlikely that the originals of those title documents may have been looted and, in fact, the same thing happened and there is no reason to disbelieve the certified copies in absence of any counter proof. He further submitted that the certified copies are admissible in absence of any counter proof. He further continued that the presence of Annexures-E, H, I, J and L in no way justify the inference of the Court of Settlement that the transfer in question was doubtful in absence of the original title deeds. He lastly, submitted that the Court of Settlement most illegally did not consider that the government allowed mutation and accorded permission for transfer which proved the admission of successive transfers and there is no reason to hold that the petitioner has not acquired valid title for want of original title deeds. Accordingly, he submitted that the Judgment and decision of the Court of Settlement is liable to be set aside and, as such, the prayer of the Writ Petitioner should be allowed. 

 7. The Annexures at serial numbers 1-4 and 6 as noted above are the registered deeds of different dates which prove the claim of petitioners about the successive transfer of the case property. It is true that the petitioner has failed to file the original sale deeds as referred to at serial Nos. 1-4 but the respondents have failed to come with even a solitary evidence to prove that the same are not genuine or have been brought to light by way of fraudulent means. Moreover, the respondents failed to turn up and swear affidavit against the same coupled with this the permission to transfer the case properly vide Annexure-F' and 'J' which proved that the Government accorded the permission of the transfer after being satisfied that the same is not abandoned property. 

 8. It also appears from Annexures-'E' T and 'L' that the Government allowed mutation in favour of the transferees including the petitioner which justify the absence of the respondent to oppose the claim of the petitioner. Finally, the Annexure-'H' clearly indicates that the Government did not treat the case property as abandoned property at the initial stage. However, the Annexure-N' indicates the inclusion of the case property in 'Kha' list as abandoned property on 26-12-88 but there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner was ever asked to show cause about inclusion of the same thereto or surrender the same which has definitely denied the right of natural justice to the petitioner and against section 7(3) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54/85). In view of the annexure referrerd to above the petitioner acquired vested right since the permission to sell was accorded to his vendor as well as to his predecessor-in-interest along with the order to mutate the same by the Government vide Annexures-E, I and Land Annexure-H practically admitted the title of the petitioner in the suit property which did not appear as abandoned property. It is true that the Government is at liberty to rescind its earlier order but in that case law provides that the petitioner is entitled to notice to defend his interest and the same having not been done the impugned order suffers from illegality which cannot be supported. Added with this section 4 of Ordinance No. 54/1985 provides that notices for surrender for taking over possession of any property as 'abandoned property' shall not be issued under the said Ordinance after 31-10-1985. In the instant case the case property having been included in 'Kha' list on 25-12-1988 for the first time it cannot be included in the list of abandoned property. 

 9. Further, the Government is bound by promissory estoppel to deny the right and title of the petitioner since it accorded permission for transfer. Further, it appears that the petitioner is in possession of the case property since his purchase and the inclusion of the same in 'Kha' list of the abandoned property without due service of notice justify the petitioner's claim that he was not aware about the same from the date. So it cannot be said that the petitioner waived his right to file the case in due time but has come after inordinate delay. All these facts and circumstances lead us to hold that the petitioner has been victim of circumstances and he has no other remedy except the protection of Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh for speedy and efficacious relief.

parties:
Md. Delwar Hossain Molla alias Dilu Molla and others.
Vs.
Abul Kashem Molla being dead his heirs Md. Salim Molla and others.
full_judgment:
Mahmudul Haque, J: This Rule, on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) was issued at the instance of the defendant–appellant-petitioners calling upon the opposite party no.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed by the Additional District Judge, Patuakhali in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Patuakhali in Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/ or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the present opposite party no. 1, Abul Kashem Molla (now dead) filed Title Suit no. 16 of 2001 initially against the defendant nos. 1-8, later on, defendant nos. 9-22 were added in the suit for partition of the suit land described in the schedule `ka' to the plaint. 

 3. The plaintiff asserted in the plaint that 4.58 acres of land appertain to RS plot no. 2381, 8.47 acres of R.S plot no. 2386 under RS khatian no. 36 and 5.62 acres under plot no. 2418 and 5.18 acres under plot no. 2419 of RS khatian no. 47 of Londa Mouja were the subject matter of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal. 

 4. In the said suit (Title Suit No. 40 of 1954) the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla was defendant no. 13 and his sister Mominjan was defendant no. 12. The said title suit was decreed on compromise on 23.04.1954 in preliminary form and the said decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The defendant nos. 12 and 13 (Mominjan and present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla) of that suit got 2.86 acres of land from plot no. 2381 and 3.25 acres of land from plot no. 2386 of RS khatian No. 36 and 3.17 acres of land from plot no. 2418 and 2.85 acres of land from plot no. 2419 of RS khatian No. 47 in their saham, that is, in total defendant nos. 12 and 13 of the said suit got 12.13 acres of land in their share and pursuant to the said decree the defendant nos. 12 and 13 were possessing, the said land with the knowledge of all. 

 8. The plaintiff requested the co-sharers for partition of the land but they refused to do the same. It is also asserted in the plaint that the government constructed embankment in the area which is known as WAPDA embankment and in the said WAPDA embankment the government acquired .305 acres of land from the share of the plaintiff, so the plaintiff is entitled to get a saham for his remaining 8.18 acres of land in his share. The defendant no. 1 denied to partition the suit land amicably, finally on 20th Chaitra, 1407 BS, thus the plaintiff has been constrained to file the present suit. 

 11. The case of the defendant nos. 18-21 is that the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan had two full brothers, their names are Abdul Ha.mid and Hafizur Rahman. Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan in collusion with the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 made them defendants in the said suit leaving the two full brothers, Abdul Hamid and Hafizur Rahman and also obtained the decree collusively for their illegal gain although the lands belonged to Abul Kashem Mollah, Mominjan, Abdul Ham id and Hafizur Rahman. 

 12. The 3 full brothers, Abul Kashem Molla, Abdul Hamid and Md. Hafizur Ra.hman and their full sister Mominjan got settlement of 12.13 acres of land from the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.Later on, Abdul Hamid, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21, Hafizur Rahman the present plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and their sister Mominjan jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Barishal for declaration of their title and the said suit was also decreed on compromise on 11.12.1956. Since Abul Kashem Molla was one of the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 he cannot avoid the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and he cannot rely upon the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 denying the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. So, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. Since the other defendants ultimately did not contest in the suit I find no reason to aver their case. 

 13. On the above pleadings, the trial Court framed issues and the plaintiff upon the issues framed, examined 3 witnesses and submitted some papers which were marked as exhibit nos. 1, 1(Ka) and 2 while the contesting defendant nos. 18-21 examined one witness and submitted the decree and the plaint in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which were marked as exhibit 'Ka' series. 

 14. The trial Court considering the evidence adduced by the parties and relying upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 decreed the suit in preliminary form on 13.11.2005 allotting a saham for 8.18 acres of land in favour of plaintiff, Abul Kashem Mollah and 2.42 acres of land in favour of the defendant no. 1 with a direction to partition the land amicably within 60 days failing which parties will be entitled to get the land partitioned through Court. 

 15. The defendant nos. 18-21 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment of the trial Court dated 13.11.2005 filed Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 in the Court of District Judge, Patuakhali which was ultimately heard by the Additional district Judge, Patuakhali on transfer who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment of the trial Court. The defendant nos. 18-21 as against the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code and obtained the present Rule as stated hereinbefore. 

 17. The Rule is contested by the heirs of the opposite party no. 1 as opposite party nos. 1(a) to 1(h). During pendency of this Rule the petitioners (defendant nos. 18-21 of the original suit) filed an additional written statement and also filed another application under Order 41 Rule 27 (1) b of the Code for accepting additional evidence. The opposite party no.1 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition opposed the Rule and the revisional application as a whole. 

 19. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed by some other persons and there were more than 106.00 acres of land in the schedule. In the said suit Mominjan and Abul Kashem Molla were made defendant Nos. 12 and 13. They did not (defendant nos. 12 and 13) file the said suit and the nature of the suit, its filing, service of summons and decree itself are sufficient to hold that the plaintiff of that suit had no knowledge as to who were the owners and who have been possessing the huge 106.00 acres of land. 

 21. The learned Advocate also submits that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed on 12.04.1954 in the Court and without waiting for service of return of summons solenama was filed on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and preliminary decree was passed on the basis of so called solenama on 23.04.1956 and decree was made final on 26.04.1954. The learned Advocate thus submits that within 14 days a suit for 106.00 acres of land was decreed in the name of the various persons and such a solenama might have been prepared at the time of filing of the suit, so the trial Court should not have relied upon such a decree which was passed within 14 days only. Over and again, the suit was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi rather it was filed by some other persons who may not have knowledge about the acquisition of suit land by 3 brothers and their full sister. 

 22. The learned Advocate also submits that whenever the 3 brothers and sister subsequently, filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in the same Court of Barishal for declaration of their title jointly with reference to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and their settlement has been admitted by the landlord in the said suit. So, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not antagonistic to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 rather, since 3 brothers and 1 sister had filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for declaration of their title and since the said suit was decreed, the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 will get more preference upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 so far it relates to the brother and their 1 sister have been merged with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. 

 23. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial Court below relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 since its original record was called for and came in the Court for its perusal, and did not rely upon the certified copy of decree and plaint of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as the original record was not called for by the defendant nos. 18-21, but after filing of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, the defendant nos. 18-21 (as appellants) to remove any sort of suspicion and cloud regarding the decree passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 called for the original records of the said suit from the Barishal record room and though the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was received by the appellate Court below on 10.03.2008, the appellate Court below without going through the same disallowed the appeal by its judgment dated 20.03.2008 agreeing with the judgment of the trial court. 

 24. The learned Advocate also submits that in the said judgment the appellate Court below unfortunately relied upon the findings and observations of the trial Court and also held that the decree of the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable without calling for the records whereas original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the Appellate Court. 

 25. The learned Advocate also submits that from the judgment of the appellate Court below it clearly appears that the appellate Court did not take notice of the tagging of the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006.The appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 did the same job like the trial Court that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 is not believable relying on its certified copy only. 

 26. Thus the learned Advocate also submits that had the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 been perused by the appellate Court below the decisions would have been otherwise but unfortunately, the appellate Court below without going through the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a ditto to the judgment passed by the trial Court, thus it is a case of non-consideration of materials and evidence on record by the appellate Court below occasioning serious failure of justice. 

 27. The learned Advocate also submits that pursuant to the decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, 3 brothers and their sister had mutated their names in the record of rights which ultimately established that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not acted upon, moreover it was obtained at the instance of others having no actual knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan bibi. 

 30. On the other hand Mr. Bazlur Rashid, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party nos.1(a) -1(h) the Rule submits that it is fact that Abul Kashem Molla, Md. Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Mominjan Bibi are the full brothers and sister but through Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the suit land has been fallen in the share of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi and since Mominjan Bibi died leaving full brother Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman and since the decretal land has not been partitioned by metes and bounds and since the defendant no. 1 denied to partition the land amicably, the plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla under compelling circumstances filed the suit in question claiming partition of the schedule land. 

 31. The learned Advocate for the opposite party also submits that Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 might have been filed and decreed but the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been cancelled through the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. The plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla has been possessing the suit land on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the plaintiff of the present suit successfully proved their right, title and interest in the suit land both before the trial Court and the appellate Court below and both the Courts below considering the materials on record rightly decreed the suit which do not call for any interference by this Court. 

 33. I have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the record of Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 filed by Abul Kashem Molla whose heirs are opposite party nos. 1(a)-1(h) in this Rule, the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and the records of two former suits being Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and 190 of 1956 decided by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal and the other papers connected thereto. In order to appreciate the arguments of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on record. 

 34. Abul Kashem Molla as PW 1 deposed that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was filed in the Court of 2nd Subordinate Judge, Barishal for the land under RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 and in that suit he and his full sister Mominjan were the defendant nos. 12 and 13 and in that suit they got a decree on 23.04.1954 for 10.80 acres of land, the said decree was made final on 12.8.1955, his sister Mominjan Bibi died leaving him and the defendant nos. 1 and 2, he has been possessing 8.48 acres of land of which WAPDA has acquired .305 acres of land and deducting the said .305 acres of land he will get decree for 8.18 acres of land. 

 35. He also stated that it is not a fact that they got a decree in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He filed the certified copy of RS khatian nos. 36 and 47 marked as exhibits 1 and 1(Ka) and the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 marked as exhibits-2 series. He also stated that they have brought the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 before the trial Court. 

 36. In cross examination, he stated that defendant no. 1 is his full brother, the defendant no. 1 is entitled to get a saham for 2.42 acres of land. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that there were many owners in the said two khatians, he cannot say the names of all owners but can say the name of Sattya Ranjan and Vabo Ranjan, the predecessor of defendant nos. 18- 21 is his brother, he (predecessor of defendant nos. 18-21) is also entitled to get the share of his sister. He also stated that they are 3 brothers and 4 sisters. He categorically stated that he cannot say whether they, the 3(three) full brothers and sister Mominjan took the settlement of the land or not. He cannot say whether they filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. He denied the defendants suggestion that they all the 3 brothers and sisters have been possessing the suit land. He also stated that his brothers have been possessing the land forcibly. 

 38. PW 3 Abdul Aziz Molla told that all the parties are known to him, the plaintiff has been possessing 8.18 acres of land, the plaintiff got decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. In cross examination by defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that the Hindu Babus were the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and the tenants that is the raiyot were the defendants in the suit, he cannot say the name of the parties, defendant Delowar is known to him. They have been possessing their land also. 

 39. DW 1 for the defendant no. 1, Md. Forkan Majid deposing in the Court prayed for saham for 2.42 acres of land in favour of defendant no. 1. In cross examination by the defendant nos. 18-21 he stated that his father and uncle are 3 brothers and 4 sisters, they are Abdul Hamid, Hafizur Rahman and Abul Kashem Molla, his father has been possessing the land, he cannot say whether their father and uncles filed any suit after the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954, in the suit land the plaintiff, and the predecessor of defendants nos. 18-21 have dwelling huts. 

 41. DW 3 Md. Delowar Hossain was examined on behalf of the defendant nos. 18-21 who deposed that he is defendant no. 18 and defendant nos. 19-21 is his sisters, 22.76 acres of land were recorded in RS khatian nos. 36 and 47, the said lands were in the schedule of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 in the said suit his father Abdul Hamid and his uncle Hafiz were not made party, thereafter his father and uncles jointly filed Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the said suit was decreed on compromise and pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 their predecessors have been possessing the suit land now, they have been possessing the suit land and they have homestead on the suit land. He filed the plaint, petition of compromise and judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 marked as exhibits 'Ka' series. He stated that it is not fact that the plaintiff has been possessing the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. 

 42. In cross examination by the plaintiff he stated that no suit was filed for setting aside the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 but Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was filed jointly. They purchased some land from Altu. 

 43. These are the evidences that have been given by the plaintiff and the defendants of the original suit. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 and considered the said decree thereof as an admitted suit in favour of the plaintiff and accepted the arguments of the plaintiff that the certified of the decree and other papers of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was created through forgery for the purpose of the present suit. 

 44. But unfortunately, the trial Court did not consider the evidence regarding the possession of the suit land adduced by the parties. Had the evidence relating to possession of the parties is considered the trial Court would have found that the defendant nos. 18-21 are in possession of the suit land along with the late plaintiff Abul Kashem Molla and then trial Court could have realized that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the parties. 

 45. PW 1 Abul Kashem Molla, the plaintiff of the original suit himself stated in his evidence in the following ways: 

 47. The reality regarding the possession of all the co-sharers and the effectiveness of the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been revealed from the following evidence of PW 1 Abul Kashem Molla who stated in his evidence in the following manner: 

 49. Pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956, the same type of evidence regarding the possession of all 3 brothers have been echoed by the evidence of PW 2, Akter Peada, PW 3 Abdul Aziz Mollah. PW 2 Akter Peda in his cross examination stated in the following ways: 

 53. The trial Court relied much upon the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 as its original record was called for. From the record of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 it appears that the said suit was filed on 12.04.1954 for 106.60 acres of land and before the date of service of summons all the defendants appeared and filed solenama on 15.04.1954 within 3 days of its filing and the suit was decreed on 23.04.1954 within 11 days and the decree was made final on 26.04.1954 within 14 days. Now is it not enough to consider the category of the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. From the date of its filing the suit was decreed within 14 days although the suit was related for 106.00 acres of land. 

 54. Over and again, Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan did not file the said suit. There was a narration about their portion made by others and the suit was decreed as it is. From a decree of this nature it can safely be said that all the activities relating to filing of the suit, appearance of the parties, filing of solenama and the decrees were made as part of a design, though there was a saham in favour of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi but that might have been done by others to save their interest having no knowledge of Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan (defendant nos. 12/13 of Title suit no. 40 of 1954 and it is clear from the evidence of PW 1 himself and others that the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 has not been acted upon for the suit land. Had it been acted upon, the suit land would have been possessed by Abul Kashem Mollah and Mominjan Bibi only but PW 1 clearly stated in his evidence that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcefully which ultimately indicates that all the brothers have been in possession of the suit land pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and not pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. Moreover, by filing subsequent Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and obtaining decree in that suit Abdul Kashem Mollah admitted his other brothers as owners of the property. 

 55. The appellate Court below made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court without perusing his own record. Before pronouncing judgment by the appellate Court below on 20.03.2008, the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the record of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006, but the Appellate Court below failed to appreciate that fact and did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. From the order dated 10.03.2008 it appears that the Appellate Court below received the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 on that day. The order of Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 dated 10.03.2008 runs as follows: 

 56. From the above order dated 10.03.2008 in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 it appears that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged with the appeal in question on 10.03.2008 and obviously, the defendant nos. 18-21 rightly called for the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 for the adverse observations of the Trial Court that the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was not called for and the certified copy of the said suit might have been created by means of forgery by the defendant nos. 18-21 and for the aforesaid reasons the trial Court did not believe the decree of Title Suit No. 90 of 1956. The defendants appellants to remove all sorts of confusion regarding the genuines of the decree of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 rightly called for the original records of Title suit no. 190 of 1956 for perusal by the appellate Court below. 

 57. However, since the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was tagged on 10.03.2008 with the appeal, the appellant prayed for time for hearing of the appeal but that was not allowed by the Appellate Court. In my consideration the appellate Court below should have allowed the adjournment petition giving a short time to the appellant for placing the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which shows the non-application of judicial mind of the Judge of the Appellate Court below in disposing the appeal. 

 58. However, be that as it may, from the judgment of appellate Court below it is crystal clear that the appellate Court did not peruse the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the judgment it further appears that it was not within the knowledge and notice of the appellate Court below that the record of 

 Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was available before him for his perusal and it would be clear from the judgment of the appellate Court below itself. The appellate Court below in the last portion of the judgment made observations in the following way: 

 59. From the above noted observations of the appellate Court it appears that the trial Court did not consider the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 as genuine as its original record was not called for and also made a blind endorsement to the said observations of the Trial Court although on the very date of pronouncement of the judgment the original record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 was lying with the record of the Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 and it is a serious non-application of judicial mind on the part of the appellate Court. 

 60. The record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 shows that this suit was filed on 28.05.1956 by 3 brothers Abdul Hamid, Abul Kashem Molla and Hafizur Rahman along with Mominjan Bibi, that is, by 3(three) full brothers and one sister. Solenama was filed on 11.12.1956 and decree was passed on 18.12.1956.The time for disposal of the suit appears to be rational. Over and again, in the said suit (Title Suit No. 190 of 1956) there is a statement that through in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 the landlord admitted the claim of the plaintiffs which ultimately establishes that the claim of the 3 brothers and one sister as made in was not contradictory with the claim of Title Suit No. 40 of 1954. 

 61. I have stated it earlier that Title Suit No. 40 of 1954 was not filed by Abul Kashem Molla and his sister Mominjan rather it was filed by some other persons. Whenever the 3 brothers and one sister filed a subsequent suit being Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 where their title in the suit land has been declared the decree and the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 appears to be more genuine and rational and binding upon the plaintiffs, the 3 brothers and one sister and there is no scope to deny the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956. 

 62. More so, it is not natural and probable that with any ill motive or for some illegal gain in the year 1956 a suit was filed in the name of 3 brothers and one sister. Abul Kashem Molla filed the present suit in the year of 2001. It is unthinkable that 45 years ago a suit was filed for any other purpose without any genuine reasons. Since the 3 brothers and 1 sister acquired the suit land from the landlord and since a suit which was filed by some other persons which was decreed against the interest of the two remaining brothers namely Hafizur Rahman and Abdul Hamid, all the 3 brothers and 1 sister to have a genuine declaration regarding their title filed the Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 and from the evidence of PW 1 (plaintiff Abul Kashem Mollah) that his other brothers have been possessing the suit land forcibly is very much significant in this Rule and ultimately has strengthened the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 in all the ways. 

 63. If the evidence of PW 1 is considered along with the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 it would be clear that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 all the 3 brothers and sister have been possessing the suit land. Over and again, in this Rule, the petitioners filed an application for taking additional evidence to prove that pursuant to the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 the name of 3 brothers and 1 sister have been mutated through Mutation Case No. 25 of 1961.This small piece of paper is enough to hold that the decree of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 has been acted upon among the 3 brothers and 1 sister. 

 64. However, be that as it may, I find that both the trial Court and appellate Court below without considering the evidence and other materials on record came to a very wrong and illegal conclusion that Abul Kashem Molla and Mominjan Bibi got the suit land through the decree in Title Suit No. 40 of 1954.The appellate Court below without considering the evidence on record and without going through the records of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 made a simple ditto to the judgment of the trial Court which cannot be appreciated rather I deprecate the attitude and non application of judicial mind and non consideration of important materials on record by the appellate Court below. 

 68. In this Rule, it has been found earlier that the Courts below did not consider the evidence of possession of the defendant petitioners although their possession has been strongly supported by the witnesses of the plaintiff himself and the record of Title Suit No. 190 of 1956 which was called for, for perusal of the appellate Court below and though the said record came before the appellate Court below before the pronouncement of judgment, the appellate Court below did not consider the same rather made a great ditto to the judgment of the trial Court. 

 70. As it appears from the record that the original suit was a suit for partition. The defendant nos.18-21 happens to be one of the co-sharer in the suit land and during hearing of this Rule they filed two separate petition, first one, is for the amendment of the written statements and the second one, is for, separate saham. 

 74. Having regards to the above decisions I am of the view that though the prayer for amendment of written statement has been filed at this stage, the same should be considered to adjudicate the real dispute between the parties and in the case of Kajol Das Vs. Monowara 8 BLC 414 it was held that the amendment of pleadings may be granted at any stage even in the appeal, or in revision. Since the original suit was a partition suit and since it has been found that the contesting defendant nos. 18-21 are co-sharer of the plaintiff for the suit land I am of the view that the ends of justice would be best served if the suit is sent back on remand for fresh trial by setting aside the judgment of both the Courts below giving an opportunity to the defendant nos.18-21 to seek the amendment in the trial Court and along with the prayer for saham and the trial Court will consider the same in accordance with the law. 

 75. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgment and decree dated 20.03.2008 passed in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2006 are hereby set aside and consequently the judgment and decree dated 13.11.2005., passed in the Title Suit No.16 of 2001 by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Patuakhali is also set aside. Title Suit No. 16 of 2001 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for trial afresh. 

 77. Original documents filed by the petitioner with application for taking as additional evidence be returned to the petitioners to enable them to file the same before the trial court providing photocopies of the same.

parties:
Abdul Malek Mollah ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md. Abdul Salam Moral and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
SAN Mominur Rahman J : Instant civil appeal arises out of the judgment and decree dated 19-8- 2001 passed in First Appeal No. 164 of 1998 dismissing the appeal by the High Court Division. The First Appeal arises out of the judgment and decree dated 22-2-1998 passed in Title Suit No. 32 of 1994 decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of this appeal are that the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 32 of 1994 for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of the suit property comprising 17½ decimals of land with semi-pucca tin shed house standing thereon, which belonged to the defendant No. 1, the petitioner herein. The defendant No. 1 purchased the suit land by a registered kabala dated 18-2-1992 and after making a semi pucca. house was living there and while thus owning and possessing the said land, being in need of cash money, disclosed his intention to sell the suit property 'and the plaintiff offered him Taka 4,55,000 as price for the suit property and the defendant, finding the said offer to be the highest offer, accepted the same and on receipt of Taka 3,80,000 as earnest money, entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property in favour of the plaintiff on 13-9-1993 and that on receipt of the advance money of Taka 3,80,000 out of the fixed consideration amount of Taka 4,55,000 the defendant No. 1 after execution of the agreement for sale delivered the possession of the suit property to the plaintiff and it was agreed upon that on payment of the balance amount the defendant would execute and register the required sale deed, but defendant was arrested and in such situation, the wife of the defendant requested the plaintiff for money and the plaintiff gave her cheque of Taka 5,000 on Sonali Bank, Rajendrapur Cantonment Branch, on 26-1-1993 and thereafter, the defendant No. 1 coming out of jail on bail requested for some money to the plaintiff on 13-11-1993 and the plain- tiff issued a cheque for Taka 11,000 on the said Sonali Bank, Rajendrapur Cantonment Branch and thus the defendant No. I took Taka 3,96,000 in all from the plaintiff against the consideration money fixed for the suit property and thereby there remained a balance of Taka 59,000 and the defendant was approached on several occasions to execute and register the required sale deed in respect of the suit property on acceptance of the balance of the consideration amount but the defendant avoided and hence the suit. The defendant at the time of execution of the agreement for sale handed over the original title deed of the suit property to the plaintiff. The plaintiff also caused issuance of legal notice prior to filing of the suit. 

 4. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the required registered sale deed on the basis of the unregistered agreement for sale dated 13-9-1993? 

 5. Is the plaintiff entitled to get any other relief? 

 7. The defendant, being aggrieved, filed the First Appeal No. 164 of 1998 in the High Court Division. The High Court Division dismissed the, appeal by the impugned judgment on consideration of the materials and evidence on record and the sub- mission of the learned Advocate of the contesting party. The High Court Division, on analysis of the depositions of the witnesses adduced by the plaintiff and the defendant and the documentary evidence, marked Exhibits, observed that the PWs have corroborated each other as to the execution of the bainapatra with the plaintiff for sale of the suit property and no contradiction could be made out through cross-examination. Their Lordships also found the payment of Taka 16,000 made through cheques to be proved and believed the execution of bainapatra in view of the production of the original title deed by the plaintiff before the Court, marked Exhibit-1 (Ka). The High Court Division observed that the defendant could not produce any document in support of his story of payment of Taka 60,000 and keeping security of his property against Taka 60,000 as alleged. The allegation of procurement of signatures under duress, and story of the forged American visa were not proved. The High Court Division also observed that the defendant appellant did not produce any document in the Court below in respect of the alleged criminal case filed against the plaintiff. Being aggrieved, by the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division dismissing the appeal, the defendant has now come up with this leave petition on the ground, amongst others, that the High Court Division failed to consider the contradictions in the depositions of the plaintiffs witnesses and that the High Court Division did not consider the petitioner's case as detailed in the written statement, the FIR as well as the three stamp papers recovered by the police in connection with Joydebpur Police Station Case No. 17(11) 93 and the fact of lodging of GD No. 1033 dated 25-10-1993 with Joydebpur Police Station in respect of loss of his original title deed No.1762 dated 18-2-1992 relating to the suit property and the High Court Division failed to consider the allegation of duress and coercion in obtaining signatures of the defendant in the stamp papers. 

 11. We have considered the submission of the learned Advocate. We have perused the judgments of the Courts below and also perused the depositions of the witnesses adduced by the contesting parties. We have allowed time to the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner to convince us by producing documents-as to the story of procurement of signatures of the defendant on the stamp papers through duress and coercion and as to keeping the defendant in illegal confinement as alleged. It appears that the agreement was executed on 13-9-1999 on the stamp papers procured on 12-9-1993 and that in the FIR the name of the plaintiff is absent. Further, the learned Advocate could not show us any reason for not lodging any complaint with the police in respect of alleged illegal confinement of the defendant. The learned Advocate also could not explain as to how the plaintiff got the original title deed of the defendant in respect of the suit property, marked Exhibit- 1(Ka). The agreement for sale has been proved by the plaintiff and his witnesses. The witnesses adduced by the defendant are mostly hearsay witnesses having no personal knowledge about the alleged illegal confinement of the defendant and the creation of the agreement for sale in reference. There is no material, in the records to show the date of alleged confinement of the defendant by the plaintiff and to show the involvement of the plaintiff in the FIR lodged by the defendant and the charge sheet submitted by the police.
