full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor of the present opposite party No.1-6 one Faizunnessa as plaintiff tiled the original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 in the court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge. Bhola against the present petitioners for partition. The plaintiffs on 25.08.1987 filed an application under Order 39, Rule I read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for an order of temporary injunction against the defendants. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing the said application passed an order of status-quo on 25.08.1987 directing the parties to maintain status-quo with a notice to show cause upon the defendants as to why the temporary injunction should not be granted. The present petitioner No.1 on 09.09.1987 received the said notice and accordingly submitted written objection. The order of status-quo was not extended further and eventually the application for temporary injunction was not heard. On 30.01.1988 the plaintiff filed an application under Order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure upon which a Miscellaneous case being No.7 of 1988 was started. In the said Miscellaneous case the plaintiff alleged that during pendency of the order of status-quo the present petitioners along with others on 21.01.1988 forcibly entered into the schedule land and made obstruction in cultivation and also damaged the standing crops ("Mugdal") of 128 decimals of land causing damage of Tk.5,000/-. The plaintiff also lodged a G.D. entry in the respective Police Station and the Police authority served notice under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but ultimately all are in vain. The present petitioners after getting notice of the violation Miscellaneous case filed written objection and denied all the allegations raised against them contending inter-alia that the statement made in the application under order 39, Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure is false, fabricated and the defendant-petitioners never violated the order of status-quo. The original Title Suit No.49 of 1987 was decreed on 04.11.1993 and being aggrieved the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.47 of 1994 in the court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was admitted for hearing by the said court and the learned District Judge called for the lower court's record and transmitted the case to the court of learned Subordinate Judge. The learned Advocate for the defendants talked to the defendants that the hearing of the violation miscellaneous case might not be held by the court and accordingly no step was taken by the defendants who are the opposite parties to the violation miscellaneous case. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola on 02.07.1994 behind the back of the present petitioners after examining one witness passed an ex-parte judgment and order of conviction of six months civil imprisonment. 

 6. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during passing the judgment and order committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the ad-interim order of status-quo was passed on 25.08.1987 and the application for injunction was filed on 21.08.1987. In fact on 21.08.1987 there was no order of status-quo against the petitioners. The trial court passed an order of civil imprisonment on 02.07.1994 but the fact remains that on the date of alleged violation of the order of status-quo there was no order of status-quo or injunction whatsoever against the present petitioners. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge is totally misconceived in this regard and by non-application of mind he passed the ex-parte order on 02.07.1994 and subsequently the lower appellate court without entering into the facts of the case being guided by surmise and conjecture upheld the order of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order dated 22.04.2004. The learned Advocate also submits that the trial court was without jurisdiction to pass any order on 02.07.1994 inasmuch as against the judgment and decree of the original Title Suit 49 of 1987 a Title Appeal was pending wherein the original record was called for and the order was communicated to the court of learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Bhola. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the violation Miscellaneous case since is quasi criminal in nature the trial court had incumbent duty to bring charge in the form of issues mentioning the date of occurrence, time of occurrence and manner of occurrence and in this context the learned counsel referred some decisions of this court reported in 12 BLD 544, 39 DLR 262, 1987 BLD 73, 13 BLD 532. 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court committed no illegality in passing the order of civil imprisonment and the order of affordance respectively. The learned Advocate further submits that on 25.08.1987 the learned trial court in Title Suit No.49 of 1987 passed an order of status-quo and after that order following date was fixed on 20.09.1987 and had there been no such extension order of status-quo, the learned courts below might not have been passed the order of imprisonment. The learned Advocate also submits that the written objection which was filed in the violation Miscellaneous case does not disclose that on 21.01.1988 there was no order of status-quo_ or injunction against the defendants. The learned Advocate lastly submits that both the courts below after perusal of the connected papers and deposition of the petitioner No. I (ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 being satisfied passed the order which is lawful and is not liable to be interfered with. 

 9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the plaintiff to the suit on 20.08.1987 filed an application for temporary injunction against the defendants of the original partition suit being No.49 of 1987. On that application the learned trial court passed an order of status-quo vide order No.4 on 25.08,1987 until) the reply of show cause notice from the side of the defendants. The defendants subsequently appeared after getting show cause notice and submitted written objection. The allegation of violation was raised on the date of occurrence i.e. on 21.01.1988 but prior to that the defendants submitted their written objection. No where it is noticed that the ad-interim order of status-quo was extended after 25.08.1987. The petitioner 1(ka) of the violation Miscellaneous case No.7 of 1988 in his testimony admits that after service of notice the defendants appeared and submitted written objection. Subsequent to that on 21.01.1988 violating the order of status-quo they have damaged the crops valued Tk.5,000/-. The learned lower appellate court without entering into the case record relied upon the Miscellaneous petition and the order of civil imprisonment which was passed ex-parte by the learned trial court vide order No.153 dated 02.07.1994,

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker. J:- The Rule issue calling upon the opposite parties to show-cause as to why the Judgment and Order dated 27.05.2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No.1 68 of 2012 affirming those of dated 28.06.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 10 Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.367 of 2001 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party No.1 as constituted Attorney by the opposite party No.2 being plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No.367 of 2001 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the judgment and sole decree dated 06.11.2000 obtained by the defendants in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 is fraudulent collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia that the plaintiff No.1 came to know about the disputed sole decree of Title Suit No.278 of 2000 on 05.08.2001 for the first time. In fact the plaintiffs did not engage any lawyer to conduct the suit nor signed any `solenama' and the defendant. 

 3. During pendency of the present petitioners as defendants appeared in the Title Suit No.367 of 2001 and denying the allegation brought against them filed written statement. They also filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint. Another application under Order II Rule 14 was filed from the side of the defendant and the learned trial Court after hearing both the applications vide order dated 28.06.2011 rejected the application filed under Order 11 Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure and also rejected the application for rejection of the plaint filed under Order 7 Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the Courts below during passing the orders committed illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial Court in rejecting the applications filed under Order 7 Rule 11 and Order 11 Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure committed illegality inasmuch as the pleadings of the plaintiffs is not correct rather it is false and fabricated. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendants do not admit the signature of the plaintiffs in their passports but the learned Court below allowing the application of the plaintiffs sent the passport for Expert's opinion to compare the signatures of the plaintiffs with the solenama and the signature of the plaintiffs in Title Suit No.278 of 2000. Admittedly, the present plaintiffs-opposite parties were alive at the time of institution of the suit on 07.10.2001 and the signature of Danish Ali can easily be obtained in the Court but after 10 (ten) years the learned Court sent the passport which is disputed; to the hand writing Expert and as such in sending the passport to the Expert for his opinion is illegal. The learned Courts below failed to consider the settled principle of law which is very much clear in several decisions of this Court and our Apex Court that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree for simple declaration that the sole decree is fraudulent and illegal. More so, the rejection of the plaint in appropriate case can be done under the inherent power of the Court under Section 151 of the Code of, civil Procedure. The learned Advocate in support of his submission referred several decisions of this Court and our. Apex Court and lastly submits that in passing the impugned judgment and order there has been miscarriage of justice and the impugned order was passed on non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice which deserve interference of this Court. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate of the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the learned Advocate of the petitioners and submits that both the trial Court as well as the Revisional Court during passing their orders committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that in the original plaint there is a clear allegation from the side of the plaintiffs that the solenama' was Obtained by false personification and the signature of the plaintiff in the vokalatnama and in the deposition of the plaintiff No.1 before the Court is false. The learned Advocate also submits that in paragraph No.4. 5 and 6 of the plaint the specific contention of the plaintiffs is such that they have challenged their signatures in the solenama, vokalatnama and in the  deposition. From the averment of the plaint it is clear that there exist specific cause of action which require adjudication into the matter-in-dispute and before taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties the matter-in-controversy can not be adjudicated. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the subject matter of the plaint ease is a mater of evidence and both the Courts below correctly held that at this stage the plaint can not be rejected before trial. As to the correctness of the allegation; evidence is required. More so, the grounds of the application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not proper for rejection of the plaint. The learned Advocate in support of his argument referred several decisions of this Court and our Apex Court and lastly submits that in rejecting the application filed under Order 7 Rule I I & Order II Rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure no illegality or irregularity was done by the Courts below and there is no non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and order can be interfered with. 

 9. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Revisional Court dated 27.05.2012 and the order passed by the trial Court dated 28.06.2011 in original Title Suit No.367 of 2001 along with connected papers and the case laws referred from the sides of the respective parties. 

 10. On perusal of the Civil Revision case record along with the connected papers it appears that the plaintiffs to the suit filed the original suit for declaration that the sole decree passed in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 dated 06.11.2000 and 22.11.2000 respectively is false, collusive and fraudulent and in their plaint paragraph No.4 is their cause of action. The case of the plaintiff's as it appears in paragraph NO.5 and 6 is such that in Title Suit No.278 of 2000 before the 10 Court of learned the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka they never engaged any lawyer on their behalf and never put any signature in the vokalatnama. They also did not prove their signature in the solenama. The defendant No.1 to that suit who is the plaintiff No.1 of the original Suit No.367 of 2001 Akram Ali as D.W.1 neither gave any deposition before the learned Court nor gave his signature therein and all the signatures as it appears in the papers are fabricated and created by false personification. 

 11. Having gone through the application under, Order 7 Rule I I of the Code of Civil Procedure I find that the defendants to the original Title Suit No.367 of 2001 after their appearance filed written statement and also filed this application for rejection of the plaint alleging that the allegation brought by the plaintiffs is false and fabricated and there is no ingredient for holding the view that the sole decree is false and fraudulent.

parties:
Nurul Anwar Chow-dhury and others ------- Appellants
VS
Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The present respondent No. 2, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury as petitioner filed the aforesaid writ petition challenging the legality of Memo No. Je: Pro:/Cox/SA/7-19/2009/ 2175 dated 23-11-2009 stating, inter alia, that 7.27 acres of land of Khatian No. 1, Plot No. 2262 originally belonged to Abdul Bari Peshker and the said Abdul Bari Peshker while owning and possessing the same died leaving behind four sons namely, Fazlul Karim, Bazlur Rahim, Abu Bakar Siddique and Abu Teher. The MRR Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. Abu Bakar Siddique, subsequently sold out 88 decimals of land out of the said 7.27 acres of land (hereinafter referred to as the case land) by an unregistered sale deed dated 7-7-1969 and delivered possession thereof to the writ petitioner. The writ petitioner while enjoying the case land on paying rent to the Government, it had gone under river Bankkhali and lost by diluvion during the year 1971- 1972. Thereafter, the case land was recorded in the name of the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar under Khatian No. 1 as Plot No. 2262. Subsequently, 54.04 acres of land including the case land re-appeared in situ by alluvion between the years 1995 to 2000 and became cultivable. In 2000, Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury made an application for leasing out the said 54.04 acres of land including the case land in his favour. Upon inquiry, the Tashilder of Union Land Office, Cox's Bazar submitted a report on 12-9-2000 to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Sadar, Cox's Bazar mentioning that the land had become cultivable. Whereupon, the Assistant Commissioner recommended for placing the said application to the "Shrimp Mahal Committee" for consideration. Thereupon, the writ petitioner made a representation on 5-10-2000 to the concerned authority for allotment of the case land in his favour. But it was kept in abeyance. So, the writ petitioner filed another application for allotment of case land under section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (shortly, the SA&T Act) as amended by Act No. 15 of 1994 (hereinafter referred to as the Amending Act). The concerned authority i.e. the Deputy Commissioner and District Collector, Cox's Bazar rejected the said application by Memo dated 23-11-2009., Abdul Khaleque Chowdhury thereafter filed Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010 and obtained a rule. 

 4. Whereupon, the Deputy Commissioner and District Collector of Cox's Bazar filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011 before this Division contending, inter alia, that in the writ petition, it is admitted by the writ petitioner that the land in question was lost by diluvion during the years 1971-1972 and re-appeared in situ between the years 1995 to 2000 and, as such, the land did not re-appear within a period of 30 years and for which all right, title and interest in the said land by the previous tenants extinguished. So, it was rightly recorded in the name of the Government in Khatian No. 1, Plot No. 2262. The writ petitioner has no legal right to get allotment of the land in question. The amended provision of section 86(1) of the SA&T Act came into operation on 13th July, 1994 by the Amending Act and no retrospective affect was given to the said amended provisions and therefore, the writ petitioner cannot claim the benefit of section 86 of the Amending Act. 

 6. The present appellants as third parties-petitioners filed civil review petition No. 507 of 2018 for reviewing the judgment and order passed by this Division in the aforesaid civil petition contending, inter alia, that they are legal heirs of original MRR Khatian tenant/ owner Bazlur Rahim. They, as plaintiffs, filed Other Class Suit No. 42 of 2012 on 27-2-2012 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar against the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and two others praying for declaration of title to the land of Khatian No. 1, in respect of 14.40 acres of land appertaining to plot Nos. 2270, 2271, 2272, 2273, 2262, 2269, 10002 and 10003 which includes 0.88 acres of land of Plot No. 2262 of Khatian No. 1, mentioned as the case land in Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010. In that suit it was mentioned that the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of Government and that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit land. They also filed an application for temporary injunction to restrain the defendants from leasing out the suit land to anybody else and from dispossessing the plaintiffs therefrom. The prayer for injunction was allowed by order No. 18 dated 6-3-2013. 

 11. He further submits that in the judgment and order of Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011, this Division held that, "there is no denial that the writ petitioner was the successor-in-interest of the land in question by purchase" which is an error apparent on the face of the record, because the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar was the only writ-respondent and he not being the original owner of the suit land, his admission, denial or silence has no bearing upon the original title-holders' title in the suit land and hence, the judgment and order passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011 is liable to be reviewed for ends of justice. 

 12. Next he submits that the respondent No.2 (the writ petitioner) claimed the case land on the basis of an unregistered Deed dated 7-7-1969, but without impleading the admitted owners of the suit land, including the case land as parties to the writ petition, he obtained the judgment and order behind the back of the original owners and in such view of the matter, the judgment and order dated 10-10-2013 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011 is liable to be reviewed. 

 14. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Mohammad Hossain, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 2 submits that on 13-7-1994 the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 was amended substituting section 86 with a new section 86. Section 86(2) provides that the right, title and interest of the original tenant or his successor-in-interest shall subsist in the land during period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of their loss. Under section 86(3) the collector is to take immediate possession of the land and under section 86(5) the collector would allot the land to the tenant whose land was diluviated. 

 15. He further submits that the order impugned by this respondent in the writ petition was passed in gross violation of the provision of section 86(2) and (5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and hence the same suffers from malice in law and therefore without jurisdiction and void and the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute and this Hon'ble Court has rightly passed the order dated 10-10-2013 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2120 of 2011. Section 86(2) and (5) of the Act of 1950 are applicable to lands what have alluviated after 13-7-1994 and within 30 years of diluvion and hence the impugned order was rightly set-aside by the High Court Division. Under section 86(5) of the Act of 1950 this respondent is entitle to be allotted the case land therefore the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 17. The provision of law before 1972 was such that where land was lost by diluvion, rent for the said land was abated on an application made by the tenant. The title and interest in the land remained with the tenant for 20 years. If within that period the land re-appeared then the tenant or his successor-in-interest would have the right to immediate repossession of the land. After 1972 and before 1994 the law was such that, whether land was lost by diluvion before or after the commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (4th amendment) Order, 1972, the right, title and interest of the tenant or his successor-in-interest was extinguished. If the land did not re-appear before the commencement of the said Order and the tenant's right to repossession was not recognized or declared by a competent authority or Court, then the land would vest absolutely in the Government. However, in making settlement of any land thus vested in the Government preference shall be given to the person or his successor in interest who immediately before the loss by diluvion was the owner of such land provided that the land re-appeared within 20 years of the date of such loss. 

 18. The law as it stands since 1994 is that on an application made by the tenant, loss of land by diluvion shall be recorded and the right, title and interest of the original tenant or his successor-in-interest shall subsist during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of the loss. 

 19. Upon an assessment of the law it appears that the original owner of the land which is lost by diluvion always had a right to re-possession if the land re-appeared within the period specified under the law. Even during the period between 1972 and 1994 when the law provided that the right, title and interest of the tenant shall be extinguished, the same law provided that in making settlement of the land vested in the Government preference shall be given to the person or his successor-in-interest who immediately before the loss by diluvion was the owner of such land. The present law is such that in case of land lost by diluvion, the original tenant or his successor-in-interest does not lose his right, title and interest if the land re-appears within the period of 30 years. 

 "In view of the use of the words, 'the right, title and interest of the tenant or his successor-in-interest shall subsist' during the period of loss if the land re-appear in situ within thirty years of loss is so clear and unambiguous that the legislature intended this provision to have prospective operation. The use of the word 'shall' is taken to indicate that the statute is to be construed as prospective only. The words 'within thirty years of loss' means if the diluvion takes place after 13th July, 1994, the tenant or his successor's right to re-possession shall subsist if the diluviated land re-appear within thirty years of loss and not otherwise. The amendment is prospective in operation and the High Court Division is not correct in giving retrospective operation of the substituted provision of sub-section (2) of section 86 of the Act of 1950." 

 "The enunciation of this rule of universal law, which emphasises that the title of a person to his property is not destroyed nor affected in any way by the mere fact of its submergency under water or any other thing, was however made subject to the following observation at page 468 of the Report : 

 24. Therefore, it is abundantly clear that if the respondent No. 2 (writ petitioner) was the bonafide owner or the successors-in-interest of the original tenant of the case land before the loss by diluvion, would be entitled to get allotment when his claim is permitted by law under section 86(5) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 25. From the review petition it appears that the present appellants as legal heirs of original MRR Khatian tenant/owner Bazlur Rahim filed Other Class Suit No. 42 of 2012 on 27-2-2012 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Cox's Bazar against the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar and two others praying for declaration of title to the land of Khatian No. 1, in respect of 14.40 acres of land appertaining to plot Nos. 2270, 2271, 2272, 2273, 2262, 2269, 10002 and 10003, which includes 0.88 acres of land of Plot No. 2262 of Khatian No. 1, mentioned as the case land in Writ Petition No. 98 of 2010. 

 26. Facts remain that the respondent No.2 (the writ petitioner) on the basis of an unregistered and unproven purchase deed claimed as bonafide owner of the case land before the loss by diluvion and after aluvion invoked the writ jurisdiction to get the allotment of the case land but his right, title and interest over the suit land by purchase before the loss by diluvion is under challenge in Other Class Suit No. 42 of 2012 which is still pending. 

 27. Therefore, it is evident that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances the judgment and order has been passed by this Division behind the back of the appellants (review petitioners) concealing the facts of the aforesaid suit by the respondent No.2 (writ petitioner). The observation made by this Division holding that "there is no denial that the writ petitioner was the successor-in-interest of the land in question by purchase" which is an error apparent on the face of the record, because the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar was the only writ-respondent and he not being the original owner of the suit land, his admission, denial or silence has no bearing upon the original title-holders which would only be decided in the other Class suit No. 42 of 2012. 

 That being the situation, this Civil Appeal is disposed of. The parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of possession and position of the disputed land. The Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Cox's Bazar is directed to hear and dispose of the Title Suit No. 42 of 2012 within 1(one) year from date. The Judgment and order passed in writ petition No. 98 of 2010, CP No. 2120 of 2011 and the present Civil Appeal being No. 344 of 2019 will have no bearing effect to decide the said suit.

parties:
Ambia Khatun ------ Appellant
VS. 
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
"the question of 'jurisdictional fact' with regard to non-issuance of statutory notice prior to enlistment of the property in 'Kha' list was specifically raised before the Court of settlement, thereby raising in fact the question of absence of jurisdiction of the Court of settlement over the matter but this question was not considered at all, and without resolving this issue the Court assumed jurisdiction over the matter inasmuch as the respondent Government failed to place any notice even before the High Court Division to justify the jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement over the matter and thus, the High Court Division failed to consider the absence of jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement over the matter. the learned Advocate next submitted that the appellant produced all original title deeds including the deed of sale dated 6-6-1963 executed and registered by the original lessee Rafi Ahmed Fidai in favour of the appellant's vendor Zakia Khatoon, and the said deed was testified to have been recorded by the official of the record room in the relevant volume before the Court of Settlement, but the Court of Settlement having been influenced by extraneous consideration did not consider this vital evidence including the assessment roll for the year 1967-68 and other documents and found erroneously the document of 1963 to be forged and created fraudulently and thus, the High Court Division committed an error of law in discharging the Rule." 

 4. Mr. MI Farooqui, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellant submitted that the question of 'jurisdictional fact' with regard to non-issuance of statutory notice prior to enlistment of the property in 'Kha' list was specifically raised before the Court of Settlement thereby raising in fact the question of absence of jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement over the matter, but this question was not considered at all and without resolving this issue, the Court of settlement assumed jurisdiction over the matter and the learned Judges of the High Court Division also failed to consider the absence of jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement over the matter inasmuch as the respondent Government failed to place any statutory notice even before the High Court Division to justify the jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement over the matter, and in that view of the matter, the High Court Division committed error of law. The learned Counsel further submitted that appellant produced all original title deeds including original deed of sale dated 06-06-1963 executed and registered by the original lessee Rafi Ahmed Fidai in favour of the appellant's Vendor Zakia Khatoon and the said deed was testified to have been recorded by the official of the record room in the relevant volume before the Court of Settlement but the Court of Settlement having been influenced by extraneous consideration, did not consider this vital evidence on record including the assessment roll for the year 1967-68 and other documents and found erroneously the document of 1963 to be forged and fabricated and the High Court Division also failed to consider this aspect of the case and committed an error of law. The learned Counsel finally submitted that in view of the relevant original title deeds on record and possession lying with the appellant, the 'legitimate inference' would be that the appellant and her vendor had always been in control, management and enjoyment of the property in question, and the finding, contrary by the Court of Settlement, must be held to be an act without jurisdiction, and the High Court Division have committed an error of law by not interfering under Article 102 of the constitution. 

 6. Mr. MK Rahman, learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the respondents submitted that the document in favour of Zakia Khatoon alleged to have been executed by Rafi Ahamed Fidai on 6-6-1963 were forged, null and void and mere paper transaction and has been created by false personation inasmuch as the signature of Rafi Ahmed Fidai appearing on his deed does not tally with the signature of Rafi Ahmed Fidai in the alleged sale deed. The sale deed alleged to have been executed by Zakia Khatoon in favour of the petitioner on 21-3-1974 is also void, inoperative, without consideration and a paper transaction and the same is hit by Article 6 of PO No. 16 of 1972. Furthermore, the LTI is quite different from the alleged LTI of Zakia Khatoon inasmuch as said Zakia Khatoon had no existence and her name was never mutated with the Housing and Settlement Department. It was found by the Court of Settlement on consideration of the alleged transfer deed and evidence on record that Rafi Ahmed Fidai never transferred the property to Zakia Khatoon or anybody else. Rafi Ahmed Fidai was a non-local and during liberation war his whereabouts were not known and he ceased to manage, occupy and supervise the case property in person, hence the property was rightly vested in the Government as abandoned under PO No. 16 of 1972; that Zakia Khatoon, the vendor of the writ petitioner was a fake person who did not purchase the land from original owner Rafi Ahmed Fidai. Zakia Khatoon was not examined in this case before the Court of Settlement and no evidence came before the Court about the existence of alleged Zakia Khatoon inasmuch as her signature in the first page of the kabala executed in favour of Ambia Khatun does not tally with LTI in the rest of the pages of the deed and the expert opined in the similar way. The Court of settlement also came to a finding about the fakeness of Zakia Khatoon and that she was a fictitious person. So, the question of purchase of the case property by Zakia Khatoon on 6th June, 1963 does not at all arise. Accordingly, the purchase of the case property by the present writ petitioner from her does not arise. Her Kabala and the kabala in the name of Zakia are products of false personation. All these are findings of facts in a petition, so the High Court Division cannot look into it. The findings of the Court of Settlement are based on facts and materials produced before it. The High Court Division could interfere with the findings of facts under its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution only if it could be shown that the tribunal had acted without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any materials evidence and facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or that it had acted malafide or in violation of any principle or natural justice. 

 15. Thus, since the whereabouts or otherwise of the original allotted Rafi Ahmed Fidai was not known or that there was nobody found to control, manage or otherwise, the property became an abandoned property by operation of law. 

 19. It appears that the original allotment of the building from Housing and Settlement Department was in favour of Rafi Ahmed Fidai, the admitted original lessee pursuant to a deed of lease dated 1-1-1960 but the alleged transfer either in favour of Zakia Khatoon on 6-6-1963 or in favour of Ambia Khatoon on 18-4-1974 was neither through a legal document i.e. a deed of lease of deed of sale with no intimation whatsoever to the Housing and Settlement Department as to the transfer by the alleged deeds and that Ambia Khatoon has also failed to produce Zakia before the authority or Court of Settlement and the alleged identity of said Zakia Khatoon has not been proved. Furthermore, the alleged deeds of Zakia Khatoon and Ambia Khatoon dated 18-4-1974 were found to be forged by the Court of Settlement. 

 20. Be it mentioned here that Ambia Khatoon filed the Case No. 1007 of 1998 for alleged release of the instant house No. 8/15, block-D, Salimullah Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka and the Court of Settlement on perusal of the materials on record and the deposition of the parties found that the alleged transfer from original allottee, Rafi Ahmed Fidai in favour of alleged Zakia Khatoon is not backed by the evidence on record. Exhibit 5 is Form 'A' showing application for certificate under Section 3 of the Transfer of Properties (Pakistan) Ordinance, 1947. This Exhibit 5 dated 15-5-1963. Its serial No. 9 shows consideration for which the property is intended to transfer. In this serial no Rs 9000 only is written. If it was intended to sell at Rs. 9000 the sale deed would have contained the same consideration. On enquiry of the sale deed in favour of Zakia Khatoon by Rafi Ahmed Fidai shows that Rafi Ahmed Fidai allegedly sold the case property at Taka 8,000. Thus, either kabala is false or the said Form 'A' is false. 

 21. The Court of Settlement further proceeded to hold that PW 1 Rahman Jahangir produced papers relating to payment of taxes to Dhaka Municipality in Exhibit 12 series; this document do not relate to the case property of 8/15 Salimullah Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka. Instead it relates to 105 of Quaid-e-Azam Road. Moreover, one Zakia Khatoon is related to a property in 8/15 Razia Sultana Road but the case property is of 8/15, block-D, Salimullah Road. The Court of Settlement upon considering the relevant material on record has doubted about the existence of any woman named Zakir Khatoon from whom the appellant allegedly purchased on 21-3-1974. The Court of Settlement also held that no voter's list or any of this sort was produced to show that Zakia Khatoon was a voter at the elections including that on Paurashava election and has held that the appellant's alleged purchase was a fake purchase and the reason being fake purchase based on some forged and invalid document also for the reason that Rafi Ahmed Fidai got the allotment for the house at Taka 3000 in the year of 1960 and the alleged purchase in favour of Zakia Khatoon in the year, 1963 was for Taka 8000 within the lapse of 3 years. But the alleged purchase in favour of Ambia Khatoon on 1974 was only for 12,000 for the house which was abnormally low price. The Tribunal also held that the alleged transfer by the alleged Zakia Khatoon in favour of Ambia Khatoon was on the basis of a false and fake document as the appellant could not produce Zakia Khatoon in the Court and that her alleged LTI in first page of kabala in favour of Ambia Khatoon does not tally with LTI in rest of the pages of the document which was affirmed by the report of the expert. It is in evidence of PW1 Noor Jahan Begum, wife of Rafi Ahmed Fidai, the original allotte that it found one Rahman Jahangir, PW 1 as the occupant of the house just after independence of Bangladesh and who as well could not recognize Zakia Khatoon or Ambia Khatoon. So, admittedly one Rahman Jahangir PW 1 was in illegal possession of the case property on 28-2-1972 in absence of Rafi Ahmed Fidai, the original allotted and considering all the aspects of the case the Tribunal held that Zakia Khatoon was fictitious a person and that the alleged transfer by Rafi Ahmed Fidai in favour of Zakia Khatoon was denied by his wife, Noor Jahan Begum and that the alleged kabalas are the products of false personation. As regard the possession of the document and papers by Ambia Khatoon PW 1 Noor Jahan Begum deposed that after liberation her articles and papers were stolen from her case house has substance and that taking the advantage of the possession of the said papers of the same house Ambia Khatoon has raised the plea of purchase by way of a forged document obtained through false personation and accordingly the Tribunal as well found that the appellant. Ambia Khatoon an impostor through improper means at least by means as stated by PW 1 Noor Jahan Begum, the wife of original lessee, Rafi Ahmed Fidai and accordingly the Tribunal held that "since the appellant Ambia Khatoon in Case No. 1007 of 1998 has not furnished facts about possession of the case property on or before commencement of PO No. 16 of 1972 and since we have held that entire transaction of sale as false and fake the case property as absolutely abandoned property," and accordingly held that from the evidence Noor Jahan Begum the admitted wife of Rafi Ahmed Fidai and on her son of Safi Ahmed Fidai that the property was abandoned by them during the liberation war in 1971 and it has been rightly held to be abandoned property within the meaning of Section 2(1) of the PO No. 16 of 1972 and accordingly vested in the Government. The Tribunal has further held that the sale deed in the name of Zakia Khatoon and Ambia Khatoon having been forged and fabricated such deeds do not confer any title and ownership in the case property inasmuch as under Article 6 of PO No. 16 of 1972 such sale is null and void. The Tribunal has held that the inclusion of the case property in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned building was rightly done and thus held that there is no scope for exclusion of the case property from such list. 

 "Court of Settlement on consideration of materials on record arrived at a finding that Nasima Khatun is not the daughter and heir of original lessee Mohina Khatun and that the said lessee has not been in possession of the house in question at the relevant time. The learned Judges of the High Court Division upon taking into consideration of such clear finding of facts of the Court of settlement refused rightly to interfere with the judgment of that Court upon a correct appreciation of the legal principle that the High Court Division in exercise of its writ jurisdiction cannot sit as a Court of Appeal over the judgment of the Court of Settlement for resetting questions of fact. Thus, we find no illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division." 

 25. It appears that admittedly the property has been listed as an abandoned property. Thus, the onus lies upon the appellant to rebut the presumption provided in subsection (2) of Section 5 that the same was not an abandoned property No oral evidence has been adduced before the settlement Court of prove that on 28-2-1972 when President's Order No. 16 of 1972 was promulgated the original lessee, Rafi Ahmed Fidai had been present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or that he did not cease to occupy, supervise or manage in person the house in question and the said position was admitted by PW 1 Nurjahan Begum, the wife of Rafi Ahmed Fidai. The Court of Settlement upon assigning cogent reasons held that the kabala of the appellant's vendor is forged and fabricated document and the original lessee, Rafi Ahmed Fidai did never appear physically before any authority for any purpose after the liberation war in Bangladesh. The High Court Division has thus, rightly, maintained the order of the Court of Settlement by the impugned judgment and order. It also appears that the High Court Division upon examining the different provisions of the Ordinance of 1985 including section 7 came to the finding that the said section can give the appellant exactly the same remedy which she was praying for in the petition, that the Court of Settlement has been given the specific power to exclude the disputed property from the impugned list. The appellant has urged before the Court of Settlement that the building is not an abandoned property or that it has not vested in the Government and that her right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of PO No. 16 of 1972. But in the facts and circumstances of the case when the State has devised an alternative forum for giving complete relief to the appellant, the learned Judges observed, she could not invoke the writ jurisdiction without exhausting the remedy provided for in the Ordinance. 

 26. In the instant case the broad fact alleged by the writ-petitioner, Ambia Khatoon is that she is the transferee from one Zakia Khatoon vide a deed of sale executed and registered on 18-4-1974. Zakir Khatoon allegedly purchased the property from the original allottee, Rafi Ahmed Fidai executed on 6-6-1963 in her favour and the said deed of Zakia Khatoon has highly been disputed and the same was neither produced in the case nor any material was placed before the Court to substantiate the sale of Rafi Ahmed Fidai in favour of Zakia Khatoon so as to devolve the interest of Zakia Khatoon in favour of the writ-petitioner Ambia Khatoon pursuant to her alleged purchase dated 18-4-1974.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman

parties:
Ramisunnessa Bibi and another ------ Petitioners
VS
Soleman Molla and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
By this Rule the defendants opposite parties were called upon to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 16.6.92 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 355 of 1969 dismissing the same should not be set aside. 

 2. The short facts giving rise to this Rule are, that the plaintiff petitioner filed the said suit for ejectment of the defendants opposite parties on the ground that Sirajuddin Mollah, the predecessor of the said opposite parties, was, monthly tenant under them and he became defaulter and violated the terms of tenancy agreement. The case of the petitioners is that they purchased the suit lands along with other lands and building from Rashik Lal Dey, one of the co-sharers of the property belonging to a partnership firm known as Laxmi Bhandar, by a registered deed dated 23.5.63. The original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah became a tenant under them who by admitting the petitioners as the title holder and his landlords executed tenancy agreement and paid rent by obtaining rent receipt after putting his thumb impression on the counterfoil of the same from the month of Falgoon 1368 BS to Jaistha 1370 BS at the previous rate fixed by the vendor of the petitioners. After some time the said defendant tenant stopped paying rent and filed a Title Suit No. 105 of 1968 and obtained an order of injunction and against the said order of temporary injunction the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 100 of 1968 and the appellate Court came to the finding that the petitioners acquired a right in the suit property and directed the defendant to pay rent to the petitioners. The further case of the plaintiffs petitioners was that the story of defendant's purchase of the suit land from one Shorat Babu and his brother Surendra Nath Biswas by a kabala dated 8.6.70 is false and collusive. The defendant now being defaulter tenants are liable to be ejected and hence the suit. 

 3. The original defendant No. 1 Sirajuddin Mollah, died after filing the written statement and thereafter his substituted heirs and the minors who are being represented by the court's guardian contested the suit by filing separate written statements-and denied the allegations of the plaint. Their main contention was that their predecessor Sirajuddin Mollah was never a tenant under the plaintiffs and it was also denied that their predecessor did not obtain any rent receipts by putting his LTI on the said counter for. It was further contended that the original defendant Sirajuddin filed Title Suit No.105 of 1968 against the plaintiff petitioners and obtained a temporary injunction and the plaintiffs petitioners preferred a Miscellaneous appeal against the said order of injunction and the said appeal was dismissed. It was further contended that the suit property along with other lands belonged to a joint business firm known as Laxmi Bhandar. About 40/50 years back the said original defendant was inducted as tenant in the suit property by the person in charge of the said property. Thereafter Nalini Kanti Biswas, son of Ashutush Biswas, having acquired the suit property measuring 18-1/2 decimals by way of amicable partition amongst his brother and other co-sharers by a kabala dated 27.7.69 and delivered possession to him and since then the defendants acquired title. It was further contended that one Abdul Majid Advocate was appointed a receiver in connection with different suits as between the share holder of the said firm named Laxmi Bhandar. The said Abdul Mojid used to realise the house rent from the said predecessor of the defendants. It was alleged that the husband of the plaintiff No. 1 in collusion with the said Abdul Mojid might have fabricated the papers by obtaining the impression of Sirajuddin taking advantage of his being an illiterate and simple person. The alleged thumb impression might have been taken by deceitful means and for which the said opposite parties are not bound by it. It was contended that the movable and immovable properties by Laxmi Bhandar were not partitioned by metes and bounds at any time and, as such, one of the share holders of the said business firm named Santosh Kumar Howlader filed partition suit No. 38 of 1972 at Khulna which is still pending. The defendants are possessing some portion of the suit land by themselves and other portion was let out to tenants and thereby they possessed the entire suit property as owners and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. It has been submitted by the learned Advocate for the petitioners that Sirajuddin Mollah, the predecessor of the defendants opposite parties, was a monthly tenant of the suit land and the building under the petitioners by executing the unregistered deed of monthly tenancy agreement (Bhara Nama) Ext. 2 dated 1st. Ashar 1370 BS and on payment of rent by Ext. 1 the counterfoil of the rent receipt. In order to prove the said tenancy, the LTI of Late Sirajuddin appearing in those documents were compared by the hand writing expert who found those LTI tallied with specimen LTI obtained for the proof in the said title suit No. 41 of 1972 as renumbered from the said original Title suit No.105 of 1968 filed by the said original defendant against the petitioners for temporary injunction. In view of proof of tenancy of said Sirajuddin, the present defendants opposite parties are estopped from denying the monthly tenancy of Sirajuddin under the provisions of section 116 of the Evidence Act, the learned Assistant Judge having not applied his judicial mind in to considering that the plaintiffs petitioners proved the tenancy of the said original defendants, committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 

 7. Secondly, it has been submitted by Mr. Rahim that once a tenant is always a tenant and tenancy being heritable the defendants opposite parties are also the tenants under the plaintiffs since the plaintiffs acquired their title in the suit property by virtue of the registered kabala of 1963 and the admission said Sirajuddin being a tenant under the plaintiffs as proved by the recital of Bharanama Ext. 2 is binding upon the defendant opposite parties, as such, the learned court below committed error of law in not considering the said Ext. 2 in its proper perspective which has resulted in an error in decision causing failure of justice. 

 8. The learned Advocate has further submitted that the plaintiffs' kabala is of 1963 and the defendants' kabala is of dated 27.7.69 in respect of the same property clearly shows that the defendant till before their kabala of 1969 for about 6 years did not deny nor challenge the plaintiffs' right and title as landlord of the suit premises and they created kabala after the institution of the suit on 22.5.69 and the defendants' kabala being of a later date is hit by the doctrine of lis pendens under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act and the learned Assistant Judge committed error of law in not holding that the plaintiffs had prima facie title in view of the evidence on record and admission of the original defendant that the plaintiffs were his landlord and this has resulted in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. 

 9. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has further submitted that the heirs of the original tenant Sirajuddin are estopped from setting up an independent title by the alleged subsequent purchase of the suit property after the filing of the plaintiffs' suit and the learned Assistant Judge thus failed to consider that suit for determination of tenancy was filed two months before the alleged title of the defendants in respect to the suit land and, as such, the plaintiffs were not obliged to file a suit for declaration of their title and recovery of possession and it is good enough for them to file a mere suit for establishment of tenancy right of said Sirajuddin, the predecessor of the defendants opposite parties at that time and, as such, the learned Assistant Judge failed to consider the aspect of the matter and thereby committed error of law in finding that the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable, is wrong and the same cannot be sustained in law. It has been further submitted by Mr. Rahim that the learned court below has travelled beyond the scope of the instant suit and unnecessarily embarked upon investigation on the question of title of the defendant without confining himself to the issue as to whether the plaintiff has been able to establish the tenancy of the defendants in the suit property. 

 10. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants opposite parties, on the other hand, contended that the predecessor of the defendants was never a tenant under the petitioners and both the parties claim the self same property by registered kabalas and in such view of the matter plaintiffs' suit for ejectment of the tenant without a suit for declaration of title is not maintainable and the learned court below rightly passed the impugned judgment and decree upon proper consideration of materials on record. It has been further submitted by Mr. Majumder that the alleged execution of Ext.2 (Bharanama) by Sirajuddin and the thumb impressions appearing therein and in the alleged counterfoil of the rent receipt are fabricated and those were obtained by fraudulent means and, as such the defendants are not bound by the recital of the said Ext. 2. Mr. Majumder has further submitted that the original defendant Sirajuddin Molla denied his being a monthly tenant under the plaintiffs and alleged that a fraud has been practised in the matter of obtaining his left hand thumb impressions in the said Exts. 1 and 2 and thereafter filed Title Suit No. 105 of 1968 against the plaintiffs and obtained an order of injunction and the said suit being re-numbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1972 is still pending and, as such, the present opposite parties cannot be estopped from asserting their own right and title in the suit property and the learned Assistant Judge has rightly observed that there exists a doubt regarding the validity of the said documents Exts. 1 and 2. 

 11. From the above submissions of the learned Advocates of the parties the points that call for determination in this case is whether the original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah was a tenant under the plaintiffs and secondly, whether the plaintiffs' suit as framed is maintainable. 

 12. I have heard the learned Advocates at length and perused the records. The whole argument of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties was that once a tenancy is denied by a tenant claiming an independent title in the self same property, the petitioners ought to have filed a full fledged suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. Repelling the above contention, Mr. Rahim has rightly argued that parties' right is to be determined at a time when the suit is instituted or when a course of action arises. In elaborating this point Mr. Rahim has pointed out that the plaintiffs' claim in suit property by way of purchase on 29.3.63 and the original defendant who was already in the suit land as tenant of the ex-owner, executed a tenancy agreement Ext. 2 with the petitioners on and from 1st Ashar 1370 BS that is, from the year 1963, and he also paid rent for some time admitting the petitioners (plaintiffs) as his landlord. The fact remains that the original defendants had no title whatsoever at that time. 

 13. It appears from the record that plaintiff-petitioners purchased the suit land from one Rashik Lal who was one of the co-sharers of the property belonging to a partnership firm named Laxmi Bhandar. The plaintiffs claim that original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah was their tenant but subsequently the payment of rent to them and then the dispute arose between the plaintiffs and the original defendant Sirajuddin Mollah who denied the right and title of the plaintiff petitioners. The said Sirajuddin Mollah brought a Title Suit No.105 of 1968 denying the right, title of the plaintiffs and prayed for an order of injunction restraining the plaintiffs petitioners not to disturb their possession and the suit was heard and the learned court concerned granted injunction in favour of the original defendant Serajuddin Mollah. Against the said order of injunction the petitioners filed Miscellaneous Appeal and though the appeal was dismissed the court directed the said defendants to pay rent to the plaintiffs. The said Title Suit No.105 of 1968 of the defendants was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1972 which is still pending. It further appears from the record that the plaintiffs in order to prove the tenancy of the original defendant Serajuddin Mollah, filed counterfoil of the rent receipt Ext. 1 and Bharanama Ext. 2 and also filed their documents of title Ext. 5 (Ka) and in that suit they prayed for proving the left hand thumb impression of Serajuddin Mollah appearing in the said exhibits 1 and 2 by hand writing expert and for that purpose Serajuddin Mollah gave some specimen thumb impressions in court. It appears from the report of the hand writing expert that he compared the specimen thumb impressions with his thumb impressions appearing in said exhibits 1 and 2. The hand writing expert found that the LTI in Exts. 1 and 2 tallied with the specimen thumb impressions of Serajuddin Mollah. It further appears that Serajuddin Mollah admitted the petitioners as his landlord and agreed to pay the enhanced rent of Taka 75.00 in consideration of the improvement made in the suit properties by the petitioners, Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder tried to argue that the defendants opposite parties denied the tenancy under the plaintiffs and alleged that the LTI in the said exhibits 1 and 2 have been taken by practising fraud as Serajuddin was illiterate and a man of simple nature. Be that as it may, the report of the hand writing expert was accepted without any objection and was marked as Ext. 20. But the learned court below did not at all consider this aspect in the proper perspective and came to an abrupt finding to the affect that: 

 14. This finding is wrong because there are LTIs of Serajuddin Mollah in the said agreement Ext. 2 and in the counterfoil of rent receipt Ext.1 were tallied with the specimen thumb impressions for Sirajuddin Mollah and it was neither denied by him nor the report of the hand writing expert was challenged and, as such, the monthly tenancy of Serajuddin under the plaintiffs has been proved. When the tenancy of Serajuddin was prima facie found by the court of law in the earlier suit, the said tenant became defaulter then the plaintiffs petitioners filed the instant suit for his ejectment but the said defendant having died his legal heirs that is, the present defendants opposite parties, contested the instant suit and the learned court below failed to consider that the plaintiffs claim the suit land by purchase on 25.3.63 and suit was filed on 22.5.69 for ejectment of the tenants when there was no existence of the defendants' title in the self same suit property by way of purchase from a different co-sharer on 27.7.69. It shows that the plaintiffs' suit for determination of the tenancy was filed two months before the alleged title of the defendants and, in such circumstances, I am of the opinion that plaintiffs were not obliged to file a suit for declaration, rather the defendants who ought to have filed such suit for declaration by virtue of their subsequent title in the property, but they have not done so. Accordingly, I find that the suit for ejectment filed by the plaintiffs petitioners is quite maintainable in the above facts and circumstances of the case and accordingly, I find substance in the conception of Mr. Abdur Rahim that once a tenancy has been established the tenant must vacate first and then he can claim independent title. In this connection a reference may be made to a decision cited by Mr. Rahim in the case of Hajee Abdus Sattar vs. Mahiuddin and others reported in 6 BCR(AD) 71. I have gone through the said decision and the principle enunciated therein is applicable in the instant case as their Lordships held in the following language; "The estoppel as described in this Section is known as tenant's estoppel or estoppel by contract. This estoppel is founded upon a contract between the tenant and the landlord. It provides that when a person enters into possession of immovable property as a tenant of another person then neither he nor anybody claiming through him shall be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to deny the landlord's title, however defective that title might be. This necessarily implies that in case the tenant sets up a claim of title in himself he shall first surrender possession to the person from whom he had taken it." 

 16. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Advocate of the opposite parties, made a strong emphasis on the question that there are circumstances which proved that a fraud was practised upon the predecessor of the opposite parties in the matter of obtaining his thumb impression in the said Exts. 1 and 2, It is a settled principle of law that he who alleges fraud must prove it. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder could not place any material before me to find that any fraud has been practised by the petitioners in obtaining the LTI of said Serajuddin appearing in the said exhibits 1 and 2. I therefore, find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate as to the allegation of fraud and find that the said Ext. 1 and Ext. 2 are genuine documents to prove the tenancy of Serajuddin and that the same were legally proved by the plaintiffs and supported by the hand writing expert. In such view of the matter, there is no cogent reason to hold the said Serajuddin Mollah was not a tenant under the plaintiffs. Since tenancy is heritable and the present defendant opposite parties being the heirs of the said original tenant they are also deemed to be the tenants under the petitioners, 

 17. It appears from the record that there are various civil litigations including a partition suit between the alleged original co-sharers of the properties of the said business firm and ending in the court of law. It is not desirable for me to go into all those disputed questions of title. 

 18. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned court below, instead of confining itself to the question as to whether the plaintiffs have been able to prove the tenancy right of the original tenant defendant Serajuddin Mollah and whether the instant suit as framed is maintainable or not, unnecessarily embarked upon investigating and raising question of the defendants' title, and thereby misdirected itself in properly deciding the real issue in the suit and failed to apply his judicial mind. Accordingly I find it a legal infirmity in the impugned judgment and decree and the same is liable to be set aside. 

 19. In view of the above discussion I find that plaintiffs suit is maintainable in law. As the present defendants opposite parties stepped in to the shoes of the original tenant they arc also tenants under the petitioners until they could establish their independent title in the self same property by subsequent purchase. Since the present defendant opposite parties defaulted to pay the rent to the petitioners they are also defaulters and they are liable to be evicted. In view of the proposition of law as enunciated by the Appellate Division in the aforesaid decision, the opposite parties must surrender possession to the petitioners firstly and then they may seek remedy to establish their title in the property by subsequent purchase from a different co-owner,
justice_names: Mr. Justice Syed J.R. Mudassir Hussain

parties:
Secretary Ministry of Housing and Public Works and another -------- Appellants
vs
Md Abu Muzaffor Ahmed and others ---------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Quddus, J: This first appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 13-10-2015 (decree signed on 19-10-2015) passed by the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Title Suit Number 23 of 2004 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The appellants instituted Title Suit Number 283 of 2003 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka for a negative declaration to the effect that the defendant (respondent number 1 herein) had not acquired any right, title and interest over the suit land by obtaining fraudulent decree in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 and the said ex-parte decree was not binding upon the plaintiffs as the suit property was an abandoned property. Subsequently the suit was renumbered as Title Suit Number 23 of 2004 on transfer to the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka. 

 5. It was stated that Abu Muzaffor had instituted Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka and obtained an ex-parte decree on 8-9-1996 for eviction of tenant and realization of arrear rent. The Government filed Miscellaneous Case Number 65 of 1996 for restoration of the suit on setting aside the ex-parte decree, which was also rejected on 13-7-1997. Thereafter, the Government filed several cases up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, but failed. 

 6. It was further stated that Zainul Abedin took loan from the House Building Finance Corporation (HBFC) on 20-7-1964 under Loan Case Number 1778 depositing the original title deed and mortgaging the suit property. He did not approach the HBFC since 1971 and also did not pay any installment, for which the HBFC authority instituted Money Suit Number 613 of 1997 before the District Judge, Dhaka and obtained a decree. The decree could not be executed because neither the original allotee Zainul Abedin nor his heirs were residing in the Country. The suit property was a two-storied building, ground floor of which was being used by a Sub-Inspector of Police and the first floor by a battalion of Ansar. It was explained in the plaint that the original record regarding the suit property was lost and another record was reconstructed and opened on 12-10-1988. 

 7. Since the original allotee Zainul Abedin was not found in Bangladesh from 1971 and the fictitious person Mainuddin was trying to grab the property claiming him as the heir of Zainul Abedin and was harassing the plaintiffs by bringing several litigations, they were constrained to institute the suit. The cause .of action for institution of the suit primarily arose on 8-9-1996, when the defendant obtained the so-called decree in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 by practicing fraud upon the Court and thereafter in the last part of July 2003 which was still continuing. 

 8. Defendant number 1 (herein respondent number 1) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit was clearly barred by the principle of res-judicata, law of limitation and was hit by section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. It was also barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence. The Government of the then East Pakistan allotted the suit property in favour of Md Zainul Abedin in 1963. On payment of salami and lease money, the possession of the property was handed over to him and Lease Deed Number 14438 of 1963 was registered in his favour. While in peaceful possession over the suit property, Zainul Abedin obtained a plan approved by the then Dacca Improvement Trust (DIT) and constructed a two-storied building thereon. He let out the house to the Superintendent of Police, Dacca City in 1967 for accommodation of the officials of Mirpur Police Station. The Police Department was paying him the monthly rent on regular basis. All of a sudden, the Police stopped payment of the rent from August, 1971. He tried his level best to realize the arrear rent, but failed. He died in 1978 leaving behind his son Mainuddin, who inherited the suit property. Accordingly, Mainuddin mutated the record in his name and got sale permission from the plaintiffs' office vide Memo Number SP-172/63/8591 dated 19-12-1987. Thereafter, he transferred the suit property to the defendant Abu Muzaffor in 1988 by sale deed number 6077. This defendant demanded the arrear rent with a request for delivery of possession, but the Police did not pay heed. Having no other alternative, he instituted Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for recovery of possession and realization of arrear rent. On receipt of summons, the plaintiffs entered appearance, but ultimately did not contest the suit. As a result the suit was decreed ex-parte. The Police Department fought up to the Appellate Division, but failed to set-aside the said decree and restore the suit. Defendant number 1 then filed Title Execution Case Number 7 of 2001 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka which was/is pending. The plaintiffs had no right, title and interest over the scheduled property. 

 9. On the aforesaid pleadings, learned Judge of the trial Court reframed the issues, namely, (i) whether the suit was maintainable in its present form, (ii) whether it could be declared that the decree dated 8-9-1996 passed in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 was binding upon the plaintiffs and whether the suit property was an abandoned property, (iii) whether the plaintiffs were entitled to a decree as prayed for. During pendency of the appeal, this Court also framed two issues, namely, (iv) whether the present suit was barred by constructive res-judicata under section 11, explanation 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and (v) whether the vendor of defendant number 1 was the legal heir of original allotee Md Zainul Abedin. 

 10. In order to prove their respective cases, both the parties examined witnesses and adduced documentary evidence. The plaintiffs examined one Md Aminul Islam as PW 1. He stated that the scheduled property was allotted to the Police Department in 1972. Before that, Mirpur Police Station was housed there. Since a new police station was constructed, the suit property was being used for residential purpose of the police personnel. Earlier it was leased out to Zainul Abedin in 1963 by the Government of erstwhile East Pakistan. In the application for lease, Zainul Abedin stated that he had seven minor children. He paid the first and second installments of the lease money, but did not pay the third and fourth. A person named Mainuddin applied to the Government on 1-1-1987 for renewal of the lease, where he claimed himself as only son of Zainul Abedin and mentioned his age 45 years. He also mentioned that the documents were missing from his custody. At the time of mutation of record in his (Mainuddin's) name, an Administrative Officer named Abu Muzaffor Ahmed (defendant number 1 herein) identified him and attested his signature. The Deputy Commissioner, however, without proper inquiry mutated the record in his name. Mainuddin got a sale permission on 19-12-1987 in collusion with defendant number 1 and thereafter, he transferred the suit property to the defendant. After purchasing the same, defendant number 1 filed an application for mutation of the record in his name and obtained an order of mutation in his favour on 26-9-1988 by practicing fraud. Defendant number 1 then filed an application to the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Public Works for handing over the possession of the suit property. Mainuddin or defendant number 1 was not in possession of the suit property, but obtained the mutation orders by fraud practice. In fact, Mainuddin was a fictitious person set by defendant number 1 for the purpose of grabbing the suit property. He instituted Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 and obtained an ex-parte decree, but no summons in that suit was served. The Government, however, filed a miscellaneous case for restoration of the suit which was rejected for negligence of Government's pleader. The Government approached the higher Court against the said order of rejection. 

 11. PW 1 further stated that Zainul Abedin took loan from HBFC on 20-7-1964. On his failure of repayment of the loan, HBFC instituted Case Number 613 of 1997 and got judgment in its favour. Since Zainul Abedin or his heirs and successors were not available in the Country, the judgment could not be executed. At present the office of Deputy Commissioner of Police, Mirpur housed in the suit property. It was allotted to the Police Department by order dated 27-6-1972. Defendant number 1 by misusing his official power created the forged document. The original lessee Zainul Abedin or any of his legal heirs did not file any application for release of the property. 

 12. PW 1 admitted that the suit property was not included in the list of abandoned property. Because of nonpayment of lease money against third and fourth installments, the lease given to the original allotee was automatically cancelled. Mainuddin was not the son of Zainul Abedin, although he claimed so in an application dated 1-1-1987. Defendant number 1 attested the signature of Mainuddin on the said application. He was the Administrative Officer of Public Works Department. No proper inquiry was held on the application of Mainuddin. 

 13. In cross-examination, PW 1 stated that in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994, they were made parties, but he did not know anything about the suit. It was also not known to him whether the Government pleader was present in that suit or not. There was a miscellaneous case for restoration of the suit. So far he knew that because of negligence of the Government pleader, the said miscellaneous case was also rejected. The ex-parte decree in the suit was obtained by fraud practice. He, however, failed to explain the fraud. He knew that the Police Department approached the High Court Division and thereafter the Appellate Division. The suit property was enlisted as an abandoned property under the President's Order Number 16 of 1972, but subsequently it was not included in the Gazette because of influence of defendant number 1. He denied the defense suggestion that Zainul Abedin and his son paid the remaining installments and also repaid the outstanding loan to HBFC, or that Mainuddin was the son of Zainul Abedin. PW 1 also admitted that after mutation of the record of right, Mainuddin got sale permission from their office. It was not known to him whether Zainul Abedin let out the suit property to the Police Department in 1967. According to the affidavit, Zainul Abedin was 45 years old in 1963 and Mainuddin was 21. PW 1 exhibited bunch of documents including photocopies of the application dated 10-1-1963 filed by Zainul Abedin (Exhibit 1), allotment letter dated 6-7-1963 (Exhibit 2), affidavit dated 2-10-1963 sworn by Zainul Abedin (Exhibit 3), application filed by Mainuddin dated 1-1-1987 (Exhibit 4), application dated 27-9-1988 filed by defendant number 1 to the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Public Works (Exhibit 5), allotment letter dated 27-6-1972 (Exhibit 6), application dated 1-4-1991 filed by defendant number 1 to the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka (Exhibit 7) and an inquiry report dated 1-9-2002 submitted by the Inquiry Committee of Ministry of Housing and Public Works (Exhibit 8). 

 15. DW 1 further stated that Mainuddin got permission to sell the property on 19-2-1987. Before that, he got the suit property mutated in his name. The concerned Ward Commissioner also issued a citizenship certificate in his favour. He (DW 1) got the sale deed registered by Mainuddin on 18-8-1988 and subsequently got the record mutated in his name in the Ministry of Public Works. Thereafter, the Government issued an order dated 23-1-1989 in his favour. He paid rent and taxes to the Government Revenue Office and Dhaka Municipal Authority. The Ministry asked the Police Department to vacate the suit property by a letter dated 20-11-1989. Subsequently, in an inter-ministerial meeting held on 28-4-1992, it was decided that the suit property would be handed over to defendant number 1. After obtaining the decree in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994, the Police Department filed Miscellaneous Case Number 65 of 1996 and lastly filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Number 1364 of 2002 before the Appellate Division, but failed. Defendant number 1 paid the entire decretal money in favour of HBFC and got a money receipt. In total he paid Taka 1,62,000. Thereafter, he filed application for return of the original documents from HBFC and accordingly those were returned to him. He filed Execution Case Number 7 of 2001, where a writ of possession was issued but a Sub-Inspector of Police, Mirpur Police Station prevented him from taking over the possession of the suit property. He denied the suggestion that Zainul Abedin had seven children, or that Mainuddin was not his son, or that he (DW 1) helped Mainuddin getting the lease renewed in his name collusively. 

 16. DW 1 produced a copy of allotment letter dated 6-7-1963 and adduced in evidence the original lease deed number 14437 dated 21-10-1963 (Exhibit Ka), permission dated 3-2-1964 for construction of building on the suit plot (Exhibit Kha), Letter of Guarantee for loans dated 16-7-1964 executed by Mainuddin (Exhibit Ga), sale permission dated 19-12-1987 (Exhibit Gha), mutation dated 7-7-1987 in the name of Mainuddin (Exhibit,Uma), citizenship certificate dated 5-12-1968 in favour of Mainuddin (Exhibit Cha), sale deed number 6077 dated 18-8-1988 executed and registered by Mainuddin in his favour (Exhibit Chha), letter dated 25-9-1988 issued by the Ministry of Public Works (Exhibit Chha), mutation of record in the name of defendant number 1 vide letter dated 26-9-1988 (Exhibit JO, clearance certificate dated 23-1-1989 (Exhibit Jha), duplicate carbon receipt (DCR) dated 30-4-1989 issued by the Settlement Office (Exhibit Neo), mutated Khatian Number 15420 and rent receipt in the name of defendant number 1 (Exhibit Tta series and Ttha), municipal Tax receipt (Exhibit Da), WASA receipt (Exhibit Na), letter of the Ministry of Public Works dated 20-11-1989 (Exhibit Ta), resolution of the meeting dated 28-5-1992 presided over by the Joint Secretary (Police), Ministry of Home Affairs (Exhibit Tha); letter dated 19-1-1993 and similar letters issued by the Ministry of Home (Exhibit Da series), judgment and decree dated 8-9-1996 passed in Title Suit Number 219 of 1994 (Exhibit Dha series) and the original mortgage deed dated 20-7-1964 executed by Zainul Abedin (Exhibit Bha) etcetera. 

 19. Mr Sk. Md Morshed, learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the appellants submits that the original allotee Zainul Abedin got the allotment by filing an application stating he had seven minor children (vide Exhibit 1).
